Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen"), not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch. When the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and boots one that is off, so do not boot a simulator yourself. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app. Build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen"), not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch. When the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and boots one that is off, so do not boot a simulator yourself. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app. Build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user. Call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and it boots one that is off and returns while that one is still starting up. Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches: the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition: 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'set_posture' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'state': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'posture' reports the state, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the state and angle with 'posture'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'set_posture' and take a 'screenshot'; if the open screen shows the app with black bars and the target sets UIRequiresFullScreen, tell the user the key is the likely cause and keep it unless they ask; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag: left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator this session already uses, else a booted one no other session is using, else the first booted one. If none is booted, 'attach' boots the only one the user already allowed, and 'launch' does so or asks for 'attach' first; if there is not exactly one, name one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

angle.description: For 'set_posture' with state 'half_open': the hinge angle in degrees, 1 to 179 (0 is shut, 180 flat); default 130.

# Bitácora del piloto Roclec

Registro cronológico de la adopción de [roclec-spec-kit](https://github.com/luiscdz/roclec-spec-kit) en este repositorio (fase F4 del plan del framework). Es un registro humano y no autoritativo: los registros autoritativos viven en `.roclec/` una vez instalado.

### Cómo se registra cada paso

Cada entrada tiene, en este orden:

1. **Objetivo:** qué se busca con el paso.
2. **Decisiones:** cada decisión, quién la tomó y qué se espera que cause en el repo.
3. **Comandos:** todos los comandos ejecutados, en orden, cada uno con qué se espera que haga y qué hizo realmente. Nada se ejecuta en el repo sin quedar aquí.
4. **Cambios en el repo:** cada archivo o carpeta agregado, modificado o borrado, para qué sirve y si se versiona.
5. **Verificación:** cómo se comprobó que el resultado es el esperado.
6. **Fricciones:** problemas encontrados. Una fricción del framework se marca **FUT candidato** para registrarla después como FUT de roclec.
7. **Siguiente paso.**

Las rutas `<tmp>` son temporales fuera del repo.

## Decisiones pendientes

| ID | Decisión | Estado |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P-01 | Componentes del perfil y estructura de carpetas | Decidida por el usuario (entrada 3): un componente `app`; `apps/web`, `apps/cms`, `e2e/` |
| P-02 | Política de sesiones | Decidida por el usuario (entrada 3): `versioned-redacted` con `secret_env` y `redact_patterns` |
| P-03 | Skills de diseño externas (`skills-lock.json`) | Decidida por el usuario (entrada 6): las 6 por defecto, 4 con hash actualizado |
| P-04 | Versión de roclec a instalar: wheel `0.9.0.dev0` construido desde `main` de roclec (`3c5e9f7`) | Decidida por el usuario (entrada 2) |
| P-05 | Aprobar las propuestas D-03…D-08 del perfil (entrada 3) | Aprobada por el usuario (entrada 4) |
| P-06 | ¿Incluir `design-taste-frontend` (44 MB, para páginas públicas)? | Decidida por el usuario (entrada 6): sí |
| P-07 | Clasificar en el perfil las 6 skills externas de `.agents/skills/` y `skills-lock.json` y `.gitattributes` (hoy solo `roclec-*` está en `excluded`): excluirlas o registrarlas como skills de conocimiento | Pendiente; necesario antes del primer `run verify` |
| P-08 | Corregir `impeccable.cmd` guardado con LF (entrada 7) | Decidida por el usuario: enmendar el commit 4 (resuelta en la entrada 7) |

---

## Entrada 0 — Ensayo en copia desechable (2026-11-22)

**Qué:** antes de tocar este repo se ensayó la instalación en una copia temporal (fuera del repo, ya descartada) con el wheel `0.9.0.dev0` construido desde `main` de roclec (`3c5e9f7`, mismo árbol que `dfc8eb8`, CI verde).

**Recorrido y resultado:**

- `roclec init` con un perfil borrador de dos componentes (`web`, `cms`): OK.
- `roclec skills`: 17 skills y 3 roles (specifier, implementer, reviewer) para Claude Code y Codex, más bloque administrado en `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`: OK.
- Registro y acuerdo de un ADR, una skill de conocimiento y el flujo (`.roclec/flow.toml`), con sesiones de agente sintéticas: OK. Mapa de autoridad generado y `check` sin errores.

**Cambios en el repo:** ninguno; todo ocurrió en una copia temporal. Los comandos del ensayo no se repiten aquí porque no tocaron este repo; cada uno se registra cuando se ejecute en él.

**Fricciones (FUT candidatos):**

1. `target_ref` exige `refs/remotes/...`: hace falta remoto Git antes de `init`. El error `INVALID_INPUT` no trae remediación.
2. El launcher `.roclec/run` busca `.venv` en el proyecto, pero el `.gitignore` que siembra Roclec no la ignora.
3. El perfil 3 no siembra `skills-lock.json` de diseño para componentes con interfaz (solo lo hacía el CLI legacy).
4. El flujo sembrado exige sesión de agente importada en cada etapa con IA (`SESSION_REQUIRED`); sin `secret_env` ni `redact_patterns` cada importación avisa `SESSION_REDACTION_EMPTY`.

## Entrada 1 — Estado inicial del repositorio (2026-11-22)

**Objetivo:** conocer el estado del repo antes de instalar nada.

**Decisiones:** ninguna.

**Comandos:**

| # | Comando | Qué se espera | Qué hizo |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `git status -sb` | Rama actual y si hay cambios sin commit | `main...origin/main`, árbol limpio |
| 2 | `git log --oneline --all -10` | Historia existente | `ec70a61` (docs y `.gitignore`), `3cd4eca` (docs movidos a `docs/assessment/`) |
| 3 | `git remote -v` | Confirmar remoto para `target_ref = refs/remotes/origin/main` | `origin` = `git@github.com:luiscdz/car-insurance.git` |
| 4 | `git ls-files` | Qué está versionado | Solo `.gitignore` y `docs/assessment/` |
| 5 | `cat .gitignore` | Qué se ignora | `.DS_Store`, `.idea/`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `.env*` (salvo `.env.example`). Falta `.venv/` |

**Cambios en el repo:**

| Ruta | Cambio | Para qué | ¿Se versiona? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `docs/pilot/bitacora.md` | Agregado | Esta bitácora | No (ignorada desde la entrada 2, decisión del usuario) |

**Verificación:** solo lectura; ningún comando modificó el repo.

**Fricciones:** la fricción 1 de la entrada 0 queda resuelta aquí: ya existe `origin/main`.

**Siguiente paso:** crear el entorno Python con roclec.

## Entrada 2 — Entorno Python con roclec (2026-11-22)

**Objetivo:** tener la CLI `roclec` disponible dentro del repo, en `.venv/`, que es donde la busca el launcher `.roclec/run` que creará `init`.

**Decisiones:**

| ID | Decisión | Quién | Qué se espera en el repo |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P-04 | Instalar roclec `0.9.0.dev0` desde un wheel construido en `main` de roclec (`3c5e9f7`), no editable | Usuario | `.venv/` con una versión fija y reproducible por su SHA-256 |
| D-01 | La bitácora no se versiona | Usuario | `docs/pilot/bitacora.md` en `.gitignore` |
| D-02 | `.venv/` no se versiona | Orquestador (consecuencia de P-04) | `.venv/` en `.gitignore`; cada persona crea su entorno local |

**Comandos:**

| # | Dónde | Comando | Qué se espera | Qué hizo |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | car-insurance | `printf '.venv/\ndocs/pilot/bitacora.md\n' >> .gitignore` | Añadir dos líneas al final de `.gitignore` | Añadidas en las líneas 9 y 10 |
| 2 | car-insurance | `git check-ignore -v docs/pilot/bitacora.md` | Confirmar que Git ignora la bitácora | `.gitignore:10` la ignora |
| 3 | roclec-spec-kit | `git fetch && git rev-parse --short HEAD origin/main && git status --porcelain` | Confirmar que el checkout local es `main` limpio e igual al remoto | `3c5e9f7` en ambos, sin cambios |
| 4 | roclec-spec-kit | `uv build --wheel -o <tmp>/wheel` | Construir el wheel de la versión del paquete | `roclec_spec_kit-0.9.0.dev0-py3-none-any.whl` |
| 5 | roclec-spec-kit | `shasum -a 256 <tmp>/wheel/*.whl` | Huella para reproducir la instalación | `9d28343e7929614ffd39346826c56ded226891486cc3c740f9fc0ec2ce698033` |
| 6 | car-insurance | `python3 --version` | Python ≥ 3.11 (requisito de roclec) | `3.12.6` |
| 7 | car-insurance | `python3 -m venv .venv` | Crear el entorno local | `.venv/` creado |
| 8 | car-insurance | `.venv/bin/python -m pip install <tmp>/wheel/roclec_spec_kit-0.9.0.dev0-py3-none-any.whl` | Instalar roclec y sus dependencias en `.venv` | Instalado sin errores |
| 9 | car-insurance | `.venv/bin/roclec --version` | `0.9.0.dev0` | `0.9.0.dev0` |
| 10 | car-insurance | `.venv/bin/roclec --help` | La CLI arranca | OK |
| 11 | car-insurance | `.venv/bin/roclec --json check` | Fallar porque aún no hay `.roclec/project.toml` | `INVALID_REFERENCE` «No .roclec/project.toml found from .» (esperado) |
| 12 | car-insurance | `git status --short --ignored` | Solo `.gitignore` modificado; `.venv/` y la bitácora ignorados | Así quedó |

**Cambios en el repo:**

| Ruta | Cambio | Para qué | ¿Se versiona? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.gitignore` | Modificado: + `.venv/`, + `docs/pilot/bitacora.md` | No subir el entorno local ni la bitácora | Sí (sin commit todavía) |
| `.venv/` | Agregado | Entorno Python con roclec `0.9.0.dev0` | No |

**Verificación:** comandos 9–12.

**Fricciones:**

- La fricción 2 de la entrada 0 queda mitigada a mano en este repo (`.venv/` en `.gitignore`); sigue siendo FUT candidato para el framework.
- **FUT candidato:** roclec no tiene versión publicada ni ruta de instalación estable; el wheel se construye a mano desde un checkout local, así que otra persona no reproduce la instalación sin ese mismo wheel. Para el piloto se registra su SHA-256.

**Pendiente de commit:** `.gitignore`. Lo hace el usuario.

**Siguiente paso:** paso 3, acordar el perfil (P-01 componentes y checks, P-02 política de sesiones).

## Entrada 3 — Perfil de Roclec (borrador, sin aplicar) (2026-11-22)

**Objetivo:** escribir la configuración de Roclec para este repo. El perfil es esa configuración: en el paso 4, `roclec init --profile` lo copia a `.roclec/project.toml`. En este paso no se modificó el repo.

**Decisiones:**

| ID | Decisión | Quién | Qué se espera en el repo |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P-01a | Un solo componente `app` (Angular + Strapi), con interfaz de usuario | Usuario | Una historia = un cambio con un run, una revisión, una integración y una release, no dos |
| P-01b | Carpetas: Angular en `apps/web/`, Strapi en `apps/cms/`, Playwright en `e2e/`, `docker-compose.yml` y `.env.example` en la raíz | Usuario | El código debe crearse en esas rutas; los globs del perfil dependen de ellas |
| P-02 | Sesiones `versioned-redacted` | Usuario | Git guarda cada transcript idéntico salvo valores de `secret_env` y coincidencias de `redact_patterns` (`[REDACTED]`); el original queda local en `.roclec/runtime/sessions/`. Se justifica en el README como única edición de los logs |
| D-03 | `secret_env`: secretos estándar de Strapi (`APP_KEYS`, `API_TOKEN_SALT`, `ADMIN_JWT_SECRET`, `TRANSFER_TOKEN_SALT`, `JWT_SECRET`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY`) y `STRAPI_API_TOKEN` | Orquestador, propuesta (P-05) | Al importar sesiones o capturar logs, esos valores se redactan si están definidos en el shell; si no, aviso `SESSION_SECRET_UNSET` |
| D-04 | `redact_patterns`: JWT (`eyJ….….…`) y hex de 128+ caracteres (tokens de Strapi). No se redacta hex de 64 para no borrar los SHA-256 de Roclec | Orquestador, propuesta (P-05) | Tokens con esa forma salen como `[REDACTED]` en copias versionadas y extractos de logs |

# Roclec coordinator

<!-- managed by roclec-spec-kit -->

## Determine the goal and current state

- A request to start or continue work triggers execution through integration for the requested scope. Honor narrower goals such as drafting only, reviewing, or checking status. A status request is read-only.
- Read project instructions, the profile, `.roclec/workflow.md` and applicable agreed references. Use `./.roclec/run --json ...` from the installed project or linked repo, or `roclec --project ROOT --json ...`. Read `.roclec/model.md` when authoring records.
- Read the project's declared flow, `.roclec/flow.toml`, and its generated view (default `docs/flow.md`; regenerate with `views --write`). It decides what you delegate (each stage's `role`), where you stop, whom you ask (`decider`) and which criteria you present. If it is missing or invalid, report the `FLOW_*` issue from `check`.
- Use `status` and `list changes` to locate relevant work. Match the request to the recorded intent and component. If the target is clear, resolve the IDs yourself. Ask which target only when more than one is plausible. Never choose by branch name or newest folder. Inspect one entity at a time with `inspect --change CHG-001`, `inspect --capability CAP-001`, `inspect --fut FUT-001`, or `inspect --release vX.Y.0 --component NAME`. For a promoted FUT, inspect the recorded decision and target before proceeding.
- On every resumption, use the current proposal digest, approvals, component progress, release membership, runs, review policy and Git state. Check any interrupted operation before repeating a write. If the goal is already satisfied, report the integration record and finish.

## Choose and execute the next skill

For a stage you run yourself, load the installed skill's instructions using the host's skill mechanism or read its `SKILL.md` in `.agents/skills/` or `.claude/skills/` and follow them. Resolve supporting references from that skill's directory. For a delegated stage, follow the next section. Keep control of the workflow after each stage. Reinspect the affected scope after writes, use the applicable gate to verify prerequisites, and select the next stage in the same turn.

## Follow the declared flow

- **Delegation.** The stage's `role` in the flow names who runs it. Delegate a stage only to the role the flow declares for it, with the host mechanics below; a role bound to `session` is you. Deliver or ask for the stage's `deliverables` (support artifacts; framework records stay fixed) and its `skills`.
- **Stops.** Stop at every stage with `ai = false` and at every checkpoint: foundation, approve and design when declared, plus the optional hooks `pre-implement`, `pre-integrate` (before integration is prepared) and `handoff` (before the release gate). You never execute an `ai = false` stage: present the subject and its digest, ask the `decider`, wait for the person's decision and record it with their real actor.
- **Criteria.** Present the point's criteria (each CR ID with its text from `[criteria]`) and let the person evaluate each as `met`, `not-met` or `n/a` (with reason). Write their answers to a JSON file `[{"id": "CR-001", "status": "met"}, {"id": "CR-002", "status": "n/a", "reason": "..."}]` and pass it with `--criteria FILE` to `change approve`, `foundation agree`, `checkpoint` or `reject`. Never fill criteria on the person's behalf, not even to unblock a gate; the evaluation must be exactly the point's criteria, an approval has no `not-met`, and a rejection of a point with criteria cites at least one.
- **Hooks.** Where a hook is declared the gate fails with `CHECKPOINT_REQUIRED`, whose remediation gives the exact command. Ask the decider, then record it: `checkpoint CHG-001 --hook pre-implement|pre-integrate|handoff --component NAME --digest DIGEST --outcome approved|rejected --actor ACTOR --reason TEXT --criteria FILE` (the digest is the proposal digest, the passed run's candidate digest with `--run RUN-ID`, or the integration record digest, respectively). A rejection adds `--corrections FILE`; its consequence defaults to the point's `on_reject` (`--consequence` overrides it; `defer` needs `--fut FUT-ID`). A `handoff` rejection can only defer, which allows removing that member from the planning release.
- **Sessions.** When you close a stage whose flow declares `session_evidence = "required"`, record the session of each role that took part (the host export is a file; ask the user for it if you cannot obtain it) and cite it on the closing decision or run with `--session EVD-ID` where applicable. `SESSION_REQUIRED` is a stop to collect that evidence: never fabricate a transcript or its metadata, and never edit `flow.toml` to relax a requirement without the user's agreement. Procedure, META.json and privacy: [references/session-export.md](references/session-export.md).
- **Editing the flow.** The flow is the agreed `process` reference. After editing it, ask the user to agree again; until then implement and the release gate stay blocked.

## Delegate bounded stages to the installed roles

Roclec installs three subagent roles, defined in `.claude/agents/` and `.codex/agents/`. Each role loads its own skills; never paste skill text into a brief.

| Role | Stages | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `roclec-specifier` | `roclec-specify`, `roclec-clarify`, `roclec-analyze`, `roclec-checklist` | Sealed bundle, approve-gate result, open questions |
| `roclec-implementer` | `roclec-plan`, `roclec-tasks`, `roclec-implement` | Candidate and run for one component, unverified ACs |
| `roclec-reviewer` | `roclec-reviewer` | One review EVD with verdict, findings, role and context |

The subagent `roclec-reviewer` and the skill `roclec-reviewer` share a name: delegate to the subagent, which loads the skill. Delegate only what the flow assigns to that role. Every stage that needs dialogue with the user or writes to the specs trunk stays with you, including foundation, constitution, UX, prototype, release, idea, amend and convergence.

- **Brief.** Give the role: CHG or release, component, approved `proposal_digest`, applicable AC IDs, allowed paths (the component's inputs from the profile), the profile's verification commands, the knowledge skills of the stage and component and the task's prohibitions. Ask for open questions instead of guesses; a subagent cannot ask the user.
- **Knowledge skills.** Take them from the `skills` section of `inspect --change CHG-ID` (per component and stage: id, path, sha256, pinned, drift, state) and list each by id and path in the brief, never its content; the role reads the folder itself. They are the consumer's own skills (reference role `skill`), distinct from the `roclec-*` procedure skills. Stop and ask the user when an applicable skill is `stale` or not agreed: re-agreement (`foundation agree --ref ID`) is the user's decision, and implement fails with `FOUNDATION_INCOMPLETE` until then. A `drift` from the sha256 pinned at approval does not block, but report it to the user. Each role declares in its output which skills it used; check that against the list you gave.
- **Host mechanics.** In Claude Code, call the agent tool with the role name as the subagent type. In Codex, call `spawn_agent` with `agent_type` set to the role name and a `task_name` of lowercase letters, digits and underscores, such as `review_chg_001`; Codex loads project roles only in a trusted project with multi-agent support enabled.
- **Result.** Treat the result as a claim. Reinspect the bundle, run or EVD it names, run the applicable gate, and continue from recorded state. Take the stage back after two failed attempts by the same role.
- **Proportionality.** Run a stage yourself when the brief would cost about as much as the work, such as a one-line wording fix, rerunning an existing check or a single small edit in one component. Delegate when the stage reads or edits many files or benefits from a fresh context. Independent review is never done by you.
- **Degradation.** If the host has no subagents or the roles are not loaded, run the stages yourself in sequence and report that limitation. Without a separate context, the review stays `incomplete` with a handoff, as `roclec-reviewer` requires; never present a self-review as independent.

| Current need | Action |
| --- | --- |
| New request or a pending proposal needs revision | Use `roclec-specify`, directly or through `roclec-specifier`, to create or revise the bundle. Reuse the existing change when the request matches it. Use `roclec-clarify` for material gaps and check the proposed intent before requesting any outstanding approval. |
| Missing foundation, design or planning | Use `roclec-foundation` to map applicable existing sources and record real agreements. Use `roclec-ux` and `roclec-prototype` when the project and change require them. Use `roclec-plan` and `roclec-tasks` to the extent the change needs, reusing existing artifacts. Apply `roclec-analyze` when consistency across artifacts needs review. |
| Missing or stale release assignment | Use `roclec-release` for planning only. Apply an agreed version and membership or a project rule that determines them. If an unpublished plan names an older digest, refresh the authorized assignment for the pending component after approval of the current digest. |
| Approved work remains to implement or verify | Check the implement gate and use `roclec-implement`, directly or through `roclec-implementer`, on the explicit component. Reuse its recorded start if current. Run the applicable checks and obtain candidate-bound evidence. When independent review is required, delegate to the `roclec-reviewer` subagent or arrange the review required by project policy. |
| Implementation is ready for integration | Use `roclec-converge`. Follow the project's authorized Git workflow to commit only the scoped changes and get the verified candidate into the configured target. Fetch the target tracking ref and refresh verification if the landed candidate changed. Prepare from a clean, committed code repo and apply from the configured specs trunk. Old or invalid evidence requires repair before applying. |

Work through requested components in dependency order. Preserve integrated and canceled participants and report their recorded state. Use native operations and preserve immutable history. For an integration goal, finish when inspection confirms the requested component integrations. Preparing a release for publication, creating tags, publishing and deploying require their own request.

## Continue until a decision or a real blocker

- Ask the user about ambiguous origins, and present source criterion exclusions and deferrals before approval. The specifier may prepare them but cannot approve them on the user’s behalf.
- Place ADR drafts returned by a delegated role under the `[adr]` folder and register them with `reference add ADR-NNN ... --role decision` before the bundle that cites them is sealed. Present each proposed ADR to the user with its alternatives and consequences. Only the user accepts one, recorded with `foundation agree --ref ADR-NNN` and the user's real actor; a delegated role never does. Before implementation, `inspect --change` must show every cited ADR as accepted.
- Present the exact proposal, ADR, reference or prototype and its digest, with the point's criteria, before a decision. Record the decision with `--criteria FILE` holding the person's own evaluation. Record every human rejection with `reject`, the real actor, reason, requested corrections and the chosen consequence before producing another revision. A rejected prototype uses the prototype checkpoint and rejection record. Inspect open rejections and give the specifier every correction; bring disputed corrections back to the user.
- Reuse existing authorizations. Record explicit decisions with their real actor, scope, digest and provenance as applicable. A draft, a successful gate, a budget or a FUT promotion gives no approval of intent. If intent changes, an approval for an earlier digest cannot authorize its replacement.
- Handle routine work within scope, including path discovery, JSON authoring, correcting CLI usage, running trusted checks, fixing implementation defects and recovering interrupted writes when native recovery confirms the state. Respect the configured branch boundaries, project Git policy, existing work and permissions. Avoid stashing, discarding or committing unrelated changes. Keep retrying only when the relevant precondition has changed.
- Ask only for a decision or input you cannot resolve from authoritative sources and existing authorization, such as ambiguous scope, approval of the exact proposal or prototype, an undecided release version, external evidence, or required Git acceptance. Present the concrete decision and the evidence needed, with the change ID and affected component so work can resume. Record the answer and continue as far as it authorizes, rechecking the digest and applicable gate. If a technical blocker remains after in-scope recovery, report the actual error and state without asking the user to run a routine command.
- Present material findings that the reviewer cannot resolve within scope to the user. Record the user’s decision to accept, invalidate or defer them, including actor and reason, and cite an existing FUT when deferred. Do not decide on the user’s behalf.
- Report the change ID, affected components, actual results and integration records. For a partial result, identify what is pending and why. Treat read-only gates as checks of recorded state. Preserve the difference between executed checks, imported observations, independent review and Git publication.

Inspect one entity at a time with `inspect --change CHG-001`, `inspect --capability CAP-001`, `inspect --fut FUT-001`, or `inspect --release vX.Y.0 --component NAME`. ## Choose and execute the next skill

For a stage you run yourself, load the installed skill's instructions using the host's skill mechanism or read its `SKILL.md` in `.agents/skills/` or `.claude/skills/` and follow them. Resolve supporting references from that skill's directory. For a delegated stage, follow the next section. Keep control of the workflow after each stage. Reinspect the affected scope after writes, use the applicable gate to verify prerequisites, and select the next stage in the same turn.

- **Delegation.** The stage's `role` in the flow names who runs it. Delegate a stage only to the role the flow declares for it, with the host mechanics below; a role bound to `session` is you. Deliver or ask for the stage's `deliverables` (support artifacts; framework records stay fixed) and its `skills`.
- **Stops.** Stop at every stage with `ai = false` and at every checkpoint: foundation, approve and design when declared, plus the optional hooks `pre-implement`, `pre-integrate` (before integration is prepared) and `handoff` (before the release gate). A rejection adds `--corrections FILE`; its consequence defaults to the point's `on_reject` (`--consequence` overrides it; `defer` needs `--fut FUT-ID`). A `handoff` rejection can only defer, which allows removing that member from the planning release.

Roclec installs three subagent roles, defined in `.claude/agents/` and `.codex/agents/`. Each role loads its own skills; never paste skill text into a brief.

| Role | Stages | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `roclec-specifier` | `roclec-specify`, `roclec-clarify`, `roclec-analyze`, `roclec-checklist` | Sealed bundle, approve-gate result, open questions |
| `roclec-implementer` | `roclec-plan`, `roclec-tasks`, `roclec-implement` | Candidate and run for one component, unverified ACs |
| `roclec-reviewer` | `roclec-reviewer` | One review EVD with verdict, findings, role and context |

The subagent `roclec-reviewer` and the skill `roclec-reviewer` share a name: delegate to the subagent, which loads the skill. Delegate only what the flow assigns to that role. - **Brief.** Give the role: CHG or release, component, approved `proposal_digest`, applicable AC IDs, allowed paths (the component's inputs from the profile), the profile's verification commands, the knowledge skills of the stage and component and the task's prohibitions. - **Host mechanics.** In Claude Code, call the agent tool with the role name as the subagent type. - **Proportionality.** Run a stage yourself when the brief would cost about as much as the work, such as a one-line wording fix, rerunning an existing check or a single small edit in one component. | --- | --- |
| New request or a pending proposal needs revision | Use `roclec-specify`, directly or through `roclec-specifier`, to create or revise the bundle. If an unpublished plan names an older digest, refresh the authorized assignment for the pending component after approval of the current digest. |
| Approved work remains to implement or verify | Check the implement gate and use `roclec-implement`, directly or through `roclec-implementer`, on the explicit component. Reuse its recorded start if current. Run the applicable checks and obtain candidate-bound evidence. When independent review is required, delegate to the `roclec-reviewer` subagent or arrange the review required by project policy. |
| Implementation is ready for integration | Use `roclec-converge`. Follow the project's authorized Git workflow to commit only the scoped changes and get the verified candidate into the configured target. Fetch the target tracking ref and refresh verification if the landed candidate changed. Prepare from a clean, committed code repo and apply from the configured specs trunk. Work through requested components in dependency order. Preserve integrated and canceled participants and report their recorded state. Use native operations and preserve immutable history. - Ask the user about ambiguous origins, and present source criterion exclusions and deferrals before approval. The specifier may prepare them but cannot approve them on the user’s behalf.
- Place ADR drafts returned by a delegated role under the `[adr]` folder and register them with `reference add ADR-NNN ... --role decision` before the bundle that cites them is sealed. Before implementation, `inspect --change` must show every cited ADR as accepted.

A rejected prototype uses the prototype checkpoint and rejection record. Inspect open rejections and give the specifier every correction; bring disputed corrections back to the user.

Keep retrying only when the relevant precondition has changed.

# Recording an agent session

Use this when a stage with `session_evidence = "required"` (or optional, when the user wants the session kept) closes. Roclec stores the transcript without interpreting it: `roclec evidence record --kind agent-session --file META.json --transcript EXPORT`. Never fabricate a transcript or its metadata; if you cannot obtain the export, ask the user for it.

## Get the session id and the export

These locations are host behaviour that may change. Ask the user to confirm the file before importing it.

- **Claude Code.** Session transcripts are JSONL files under `~/.claude/projects/<project-folder>/<session-id>.jsonl`. The session id is shown by `/status`.
- **Codex.** Rollout JSONL files live under `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl`; the session id is part of the file name and of its first record.

A delegated role reports its own host and session id in its output; the coordinator maps it to the export of that session.

## Fill META.json

Do not declare `kind`; the command sets it.

```json
{
  "model_schema": 2,
  "host": "claude-code",
  "host_session_id": "id from the host",
  "actor": "who ran the session",
  "role": "specifier|implementer|reviewer|coordinator|agent role declared in flow.toml",
  "model": "model that ran it",
  "started_at": "2026-01-01T10:00:00Z",
  "ended_at": "2026-01-01T11:00:00Z",
  "stage": "flow stage name",
  "change_id": "CHG-001",
  "component": "NAME"
}
```

- Times are UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`; `ended_at` is not before `started_at`. Take them from the export, not from memory.
- Scope by stage: `change_id` for every stage except foundation and release, plus `component` for design, implement, verify, review and integrate (optional for define, approve and plan). A define session may name a CHG id not imported yet. Foundation uses `subject` (the reference or ADR id) instead. Release uses `release` `{"component": "NAME", "version": "vX.Y.0"}`.
- Cite the resulting EVD id with `--session EVD-...` (repeatable) on the closing record: `change approve|cancel|start`, `foundation agree`, `reject`, `checkpoint`, `fut decide` and `run verify`. An independent review cites the reviewer's session as its `context` when the review stage requires sessions.

## Privacy

Transcripts contain code, paths, names and possibly personal data. Redaction covers only the profile's configured `secret_env` values and `redact_patterns`; it does not find anything else. Before versioning, review `[sessions] storage` in the profile: `versioned-redacted` (default), `local` (nothing versioned) or `versioned-raw` (may contain secrets). Choose `local` when in doubt. A transcript over `quota_bytes` is rejected, never truncated.

# Recording an agent session

Use this when a stage with `session_evidence = "required"` (or optional, when the user wants the session kept) closes. Roclec stores the transcript without interpreting it: `roclec evidence record --kind agent-session --file META.json --transcript EXPORT`. Never fabricate a transcript or its metadata; if you cannot obtain the export, ask the user for it.

## Get the session id and the export

These locations are host behaviour that may change. Ask the user to confirm the file before importing it.

- **Claude Code.** Session transcripts are JSONL files under `~/.claude/projects/<project-folder>/<session-id>.jsonl`. The session id is shown by `/status`.
- **Codex.** Rollout JSONL files live under `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl`; the session id is part of the file name and of its first record.

A delegated role reports its own host and session id in its output; the coordinator maps it to the export of that session.

## Fill META.json

Do not declare `kind`; the command sets it.

```json
{
  "model_schema": 2,
  "host": "claude-code",
  "host_session_id": "id from the host",
  "actor": "who ran the session",
  "role": "specifier|implementer|reviewer|coordinator|agent role declared in flow.toml",
  "model": "model that ran it",
  "started_at": "2026-01-01T10:00:00Z",
  "ended_at": "2026-01-01T11:00:00Z",
  "stage": "flow stage name",
  "change_id": "CHG-001",
  "component": "NAME"
}
```

- Times are UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`; `ended_at` is not before `started_at`. Take them from the export, not from memory.
- Scope by stage: `change_id` for every stage except foundation and release, plus `component` for design, implement, verify, review and integrate (optional for define, approve and plan). A define session may name a CHG id not imported yet. Foundation uses `subject` (the reference or ADR id) instead. Release uses `release` `{"component": "NAME", "version": "vX.Y.0"}`.
- Cite the resulting EVD id with `--session EVD-...` (repeatable) on the closing record: `change approve|cancel|start`, `foundation agree`, `reject`, `checkpoint`, `fut decide` and `run verify`. An independent review cites the reviewer's session as its `context` when the review stage requires sessions.

## Privacy

Transcripts contain code, paths, names and possibly personal data. Redaction covers only the profile's configured `secret_env` values and `redact_patterns`; it does not find anything else. Before versioning, review `[sessions] storage` in the profile: `versioned-redacted` (default), `local` (nothing versioned) or `versioned-raw` (may contain secrets). Choose `local` when in doubt. A transcript over `quota_bytes` is rejected, never truncated.

# Roclec foundation

<!-- managed by roclec-spec-kit -->

Read project instructions, `.roclec/project.toml` (schema 3), `.roclec/workflow.md` and applicable agreed references. Inspect with `inspect --change CHG-001`, `inspect --capability CAP-001`, or `inspect --release vX.Y.0 --component NAME`; never guess from branches or the newest folder.

Preserve consumer-owned templates, identities, decisions and immutable history. Contracts live in snapshots and current.json; release.json alone owns membership. Status is derived, never an editable done field. Read `.roclec/model.md` when authoring JSON. Passing structural checks does not establish semantic sufficiency or user approval. Complete the authorized scope; ask only for unresolved material decisions. Report actual evidence, limitations and one useful next action without executing an unauthorized action.

Inventory existing context, principles, architecture/stack, engineering, verification, operations and applicable design authorities. Map existing documents rather than creating duplicate truths. Distinguish proposals, agreements and unresolved decisions, with actor/reason and source hashes. Register sources with `reference add ID --path PATH --component NAME --role ROLE` or `reference update`. Record an actual agreement with `foundation agree --ref ID --actor ACTOR --reason REASON --criteria FILE` (the user's per-criterion evaluation of the foundation point of the flow; see the coordinator). For user-facing design consult consumer-pinned design skills when relevant; restore only an existing consumer skills-lock.json when authorized, without guessing a stack. Run `foundation check --component NAME [--change CHG-ID]`. A passing existence/hash check does not certify semantic sufficiency; resolve material gaps before implementation.

Inventory existing architecture decisions too. Register each ADR file under the profile's `[adr]` folder (default `docs/adr/`) as it is, with `reference add ADR-NNN --path PATH --component NAME --role decision [--supersedes ADR-MMM]`; do not rewrite it into the template. An ADR's state (proposed, accepted, stale, superseded) is derived: read it with `list adrs` or `inspect --adr ADR-NNN`. Only `foundation agree --ref ADR-NNN` with the user's real actor and criteria evaluation accepts one, and only after the user decided it. ADRs are not foundation roles that every component needs, and they are not `.roclec/decisions/`, which holds approvals and agreements.

Seed or adapt the project flow with the user: `.roclec/flow.toml` is project-owned (seeded by `init`/`skills`, preserved by refreshes) and holds roles (`[roles.NAME] kind = human|agent`), criteria (`[criteria.CR-NNN] text`) and the ten stages with `ai` (false requires `reason`), `role`, optional `deliverables`, `session_evidence`, `skills` and `checkpoint = { decider, criteria, on_reject }`. Foundation, approve and design always carry a checkpoint and approve is always `ai = false`. Do not invent criteria; propose wording and let the user decide. Run `views --write` to generate the readable view and `check` to confirm no `FLOW_*` warning. Register the flow as the `process` reference for every component: `reference add flow --path .roclec/flow.toml --role process --component NAME`, then ask the user to agree with the exact points' criteria: `foundation agree --ref flow --actor ACTOR --reason TEXT --criteria FILE`, where FILE is the user's own evaluation `[{"id": "CR-001", "status": "met"}]`. description: Establish or revise agreed product, engineering and design references for native Roclec components.

# Roclec foundation

<!-- managed by roclec-spec-kit -->

Read project instructions, `.roclec/project.toml` (schema 3), `.roclec/workflow.md` and applicable agreed references. Use `./.roclec/run --json ...` or `roclec --project ROOT --json ...`; the launcher supplies the project root. Select explicit CHG/CAP/FUT/release and component for mutations. Inspect with `inspect --change CHG-001`, `inspect --capability CAP-001`, or `inspect --release vX.Y.0 --component NAME`; never guess from branches or the newest folder.

Preserve consumer-owned templates, identities, decisions and immutable history. Contracts live in snapshots and current.json; release.json alone owns membership. Status is derived, never an editable done field. Read `.roclec/model.md` when authoring JSON. Passing structural checks does not establish semantic sufficiency or user approval. Complete the authorized scope; ask only for unresolved material decisions. Report actual evidence, limitations and one useful next action without executing an unauthorized action.

Inventory existing context, principles, architecture/stack, engineering, verification, operations and applicable design authorities. Map existing documents rather than creating duplicate truths. Distinguish proposals, agreements and unresolved decisions, with actor/reason and source hashes. Register sources with `reference add ID --path PATH --component NAME --role ROLE` or `reference update`. Record an actual agreement with `foundation agree --ref ID --actor ACTOR --reason REASON --criteria FILE` (the user's per-criterion evaluation of the foundation point of the flow; see the coordinator). For user-facing design consult consumer-pinned design skills when relevant; restore only an existing consumer skills-lock.json when authorized, without guessing a stack. Run `foundation check --component NAME [--change CHG-ID]`. A passing existence/hash check does not certify semantic sufficiency; resolve material gaps before implementation.

Inventory existing architecture decisions too. Register each ADR file under the profile's `[adr]` folder (default `docs/adr/`) as it is, with `reference add ADR-NNN --path PATH --component NAME --role decision [--supersedes ADR-MMM]`; do not rewrite it into the template. An ADR's state (proposed, accepted, stale, superseded) is derived: read it with `list adrs` or `inspect --adr ADR-NNN`. Only `foundation agree --ref ADR-NNN` with the user's real actor and criteria evaluation accepts one, and only after the user decided it. ADRs are not foundation roles that every component needs, and they are not `.roclec/decisions/`, which holds approvals and agreements.

Seed or adapt the project flow with the user: `.roclec/flow.toml` is project-owned (seeded by `init`/`skills`, preserved by refreshes) and holds roles (`[roles.NAME] kind = human|agent`), criteria (`[criteria.CR-NNN] text`) and the ten stages with `ai` (false requires `reason`), `role`, optional `deliverables`, `session_evidence`, `skills` and `checkpoint = { decider, criteria, on_reject }`. Ask which stages the user decides themselves, who the deciders are, which criteria they judge by and whether to add the optional hooks (implement = pre-implement, integrate = pre-integrate, release = handoff; a handoff checkpoint must use `on_reject = "defer"`). Foundation, approve and design always carry a checkpoint and approve is always `ai = false`. Do not invent criteria; propose wording and let the user decide. Run `views --write` to generate the readable view and `check` to confirm no `FLOW_*` warning. Register the flow as the `process` reference for every component: `reference add flow --path .roclec/flow.toml --role process --component NAME`, then ask the user to agree with the exact points' criteria: `foundation agree --ref flow --actor ACTOR --reason TEXT --criteria FILE`, where FILE is the user's own evaluation `[{"id": "CR-001", "status": "met"}]`. Editing the flow afterwards needs a new agreement before implement or release: cite the open process FUTs it addresses with `foundation agree --ref flow ... --fut FUT-NNN` (repeatable), record the foundation session (see `roclec-coordinator`), run `views --write` to refresh the flow view and its "Flow learning", and point the user to `docs/flow-retro.md` for their own reflection. Promote an addressed FUT with `fut decide FUT --outcome promoted --target DECISION_ID`.

Knowledge skills are the project's own reusable knowledge for agents, owned by the consumer; procedure skills `roclec-*` are owned by Roclec and refreshed by `roclec skills`. A knowledge skill is a reference with role `skill` whose canonical folder is `.agents/skills/ID/` with a `SKILL.md`; the ID is lowercase and never starts with `roclec-` or `speckit-`. Inventory the project's own skills: folders under `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` that are not `roclec-*` or `speckit-*`, and every `SKILL_UNREGISTERED` warning from `check` (an own skill neither registered nor in `skills-lock.json`). Propose registering each one; move one found only under `.claude/skills/` to `.agents/skills/ID/` first, because the `.claude/skills/` copy is generated and never the source. Register it with `reference add ID --path .agents/skills/ID --role skill --component NAME` (repeat `--component` for every component it applies to) and ask the user to agree it with `foundation agree --ref ID --actor ACTOR --reason REASON --criteria FILE`. The agreement pins every file of the folder: any edit makes it `stale` until agreed again, and symlinks are rejected. To capture new knowledge offer `.roclec/templates/skill-template.md` (Purpose, Applies to, Authority, Conventions or procedure, Examples, Verification); the skill cites the references and ADRs it applies under Authority and does not restate them. To limit a skill to stages, list it in `skills = ["ID"]` of those stages in `.roclec/flow.toml` (each must be a registered skill reference, else `FLOW_SKILL_UNREGISTERED`); a skill no stage lists applies to every stage of its components. After registering or agreeing, run `roclec skills` (or `views --write`) so the authority map in the managed block of `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` and the `.claude/skills/` copies are current; `check` warns `AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS_STALE`, `SKILL_COPY_DIVERGED` and `SKILL_UNREGISTERED`. Never edit the `.claude/skills/` copy: refresh refuses an edited copy with `MANAGED_FILE_EDITED`.

# Agentic Flow Requirements

The expected solution is an **agentic flow**: a system of AI agents that takes the user stories to QA-ready code, with people stepping in at the points you define. We do not give you the order or composition of the flow; designing it is part of the test.

## Mandatory requirements

- **Subagents.** The flow uses subagents with separate responsibilities. Their definitions (instructions, allowed tools, inputs and outputs) are versioned in the repository.
- **Skills.** The flow uses at least one custom skill, versioned in the repository, that encapsulates reusable project knowledge (for example conventions, templates or procedures).
- **Context file.** There is a global context file (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or equivalent) with the conventions all agents must follow.
- **ADRs.** Relevant architecture decisions are recorded in ADRs (MADR, Nygard or similar format), with context, alternatives considered and consequences. At minimum, one on the multi-country strategy.
- **Specs.** Each user story has its spec before it is implemented.
- **Code review.** There is evidence of code review within the flow, with findings and how they were resolved.
- **Traceability.** The thread user story → spec → ADR → code → tests → review can be followed.

## Suggestions

- We suggest, though it is not mandatory, using **Spec-Driven Development (SDD)**: the spec is the source of truth and the code is derived from it. You may use an SDD framework (for example Spec Kit, Kiro or another) or your own variant, but explain why.
- The tool is your choice: Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Codex or another. **Justify your choice.**

## Step by step: from functional user story to QA handoff

You must deliver a `FLOW.md` file that explains your full flow, from receiving a functional user story until the increment is ready for QA. Include a **diagram of the flow** (Mermaid or image).

For **each step** of the flow, document at least the following:

| Step | Description | AI used? | AI, agent, subagent or skill used | Deliverable produced | Human in the loop |
|------|-------------|----------|-----------------------------------|----------------------|-------------------|
| *Step name* | *What happens and why* | *Yes / No* | *Tool, model and component* | *File or artifact produced (path in the repo)* | *Who steps in, what they review or approve, and what happens on rejection* |

This table is only the minimum format: you define the number, order and content of the steps.

### Questions to answer briefly in `FLOW.md`

- What you would do differently if a team of 5 developers used this flow.
- Which part of the flow did not work as expected and how you adjusted it.
- At which points you decided not to use AI and why.
# Evaluation Criteria

**65%** of the score covers the agentic flow and its artifacts; **35%** covers the application.

| Criterion | What we look at | Weight |
|-----------|-----------------|--------|
| Agentic flow design | Clear responsibilities per subagent, defined inputs and outputs, skills with real value, a context file that governs generation | 20% |
| Human in the loop and control | Justified checkpoints, approval or rejection criteria, evidence that the person corrected the agent | 15% |
| Specs and ADRs | Specs that detect gaps in the user story and make it verifiable; ADRs with real alternatives and consequences | 15% |
| Review and verification | Real findings in reviews, traceable fixes, tests that validate behavior | 15% |
| Multi-country strategy and configurability | Content differentiated by country without duplicating the app; form and plans 100% configurable from Strapi | 15% |
| Angular and Strapi technical quality | Modern Angular, typing, loading and error state handling, token and permission security | 10% |
| Communication | Clarity of `FLOW.md` and README | 10% |

| 9 | integrate | sí | coordinator | — *(gancho opcional pre-integrate)* | — | — |

Todas las etapas con IA tienen `session_evidence = "required"`. Un único rol humano: `owner`.

Criterios sembrados:
- CR-001 «The reference reflects the practice the user agreed.»
- CR-002 «Every origin criterion is covered, excluded or deferred.»
- CR-003 «The proposal states the intended behavior.»
- CR-004 «The prototype matches the approved intention.»

**Contexto del assessment:** 15 % de la nota es «checkpoints justificados, criterios de aprobación/rechazo, evidencia de que la persona corrigió al agente». Los criterios sembrados son genéricos. `FLOW.md` además pide en qué puntos se decidió no usar IA y por qué.

- foundation: CR-001 + **CR-005** «The reference is consistent with `docs/assessment/` and with references already agreed.»
- approve: CR-002, CR-003 + **CR-006** «Every acceptance criterion is verifiable by an automated test (unit or e2e).» + **CR-007** «The proposal cites the ADRs it applies.»
- design: CR-004 + **CR-008** «The prototype covers loading, error and empty states for both countries.»

.roclec/workflow.md:8:The project flow, `.roclec/flow.toml`, declares the ten stages (foundation, define, approve, design, plan, implement, verify, review, integrate, release) with each stage's `role`, `ai` (false requires a `reason`), optional `deliverables`, `skills` and `session_evidence`, and the human checkpoints with their `decider`, `criteria` (CR IDs with text under `[criteria]`) and `on_reject` (`revise`, `cancel` or `defer`). The coordinator delegates by `role` and stops at every checkpoint and every `ai = false` stage; approve is always `ai = false`. Foundation, approve and design carry a checkpoint. Implement, integrate and release may carry an optional hook (`pre-implement`, `pre-integrate`, `handoff`); a handoff checkpoint must use `on_reject = "defer"`. The flow is project-owned (seeded once, preserved by refreshes) and is agreed as the reference with role `process`: `reference add flow --path .roclec/flow.toml --role process --component NAME` for every component, then `foundation agree --ref flow ...`. Editing it afterwards blocks the implement gate and the release gate until it is agreed again. `views --write` generates the readable view (default `docs/flow.md`); `check` warns `FLOW_VIEW_STALE`, `FLOW_MISSING` and similar.
.roclec/workflow.md:10:Every decision at a declared point takes `--criteria FILE`, the person's own JSON evaluation `[{"id": "CR-001", "status": "met|not-met|n/a", "reason": "..."}]` of exactly the criteria declared for that point (`n/a` needs a reason; an approval has no `not-met`; a rejection of a point that declares criteria cites at least one `not-met`). Commands: `change approve`, `foundation agree`, `checkpoint` and `reject`. Points: `change approve` and `reject change` use `approve`; `foundation agree` and `reject adr|reference` use `foundation`; prototype `checkpoint` and `reject prototype` use `design`; hook checkpoints use their hook. `--consequence` defaults to the point's `on_reject`. Hook checkpoints are `checkpoint CHG-ID --hook pre-implement|pre-integrate|handoff --component NAME --digest DIGEST --outcome approved|rejected --actor ACTOR --reason TEXT --criteria FILE [--run RUN-ID] [--corrections FILE --consequence C --fut FUT-ID]`, with DIGEST the proposal digest, the passed run's candidate `inputs_digest` (with `--run`) or the integration record digest. A declared hook blocks its gates until approved: `pre-implement` the implement, verify and integrate gates; `pre-integrate` the integrate gate and `integrate prepare`; `handoff` the release gate and `release prepare`, all with `CHECKPOINT_REQUIRED`, whose remediation names the exact command. A handoff rejection is only `defer`, with a FUT, and then allows removing that member from the planning release. Neither the gate nor an agent can record these decisions on the person's behalf.
.roclec/workflow.md:12:Knowledge skills are the consumer's own references with role `skill` in `.agents/skills/ID/`, distinct from the `roclec-*` skills Roclec refreshes. Register one with `reference add ID --path .agents/skills/ID --role skill --component NAME` and have the user agree it with `foundation agree --ref ID --actor ACTOR --reason TEXT --criteria FILE`; any edit to the folder makes it stale until agreed again. `change approve` pins every skill of the change's components, at any stage, in the decision. Implement requires every skill registered for the component, whatever its stages, agreed on its current bytes (`FOUNDATION_INCOMPLETE`); `inspect --change CHG-ID` lists them per component and stage, and the coordinator gives each role those skills by id and path. `roclec skills` copies them to `.claude/skills/` and regenerates the authority map in the managed block of `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`; never edit the copies.
.roclec/workflow.md:18:Sources: references.json links agreed existing documents; contracts/<CAP>/<SHA> contains immutable snapshots; current.json alone maps integrated component/capability revisions. Changes contain intent, exact bases, normative deltas and proposed snapshots. Approval freezes that digest. A new semantic revision needs a new approval; integrated participants preserve their original intent and cannot be redefined by pending work. FUT captures discovery, not approval. Each approved change declares its sources, captured Markdown and criterion-to-AC coverage. Capture only necessary source text and redact personal data before sealing. Inspect the change to review mappings and use `list changes --origin ID` to find related changes. ADR references (role `decision`, ID ADR-NNN) have a derived state listed by `list adrs`; only `foundation agree` by the user accepts one, and a later agreed ADR that declares `supersedes` replaces it for new changes. The release gate reports members that applied a since-superseded ADR as `limitations` without blocking.
.roclec/model.md:13:- `origins` contains entries with `kind`, `id`, `locator`, `captured` and `criteria`. The supported kinds are `fut|story|issue|incident|request`. Use an ID unique within the change, a source location, a relative Markdown capture path and sorted, unique criterion IDs. A request also requires `actor`. At least one origin is required for approval. `change seal` adds each captured path to `files` and hashes its bytes. The consumer is responsible for the captured content. Include only needed text and redact personal data before sealing.
.roclec/model.md:14:- `coverage` contains `criteria` and `derived`. Each criterion entry names `origin` and `criterion` and has exactly one status. Use `covered` with sorted, unique, nonempty `acceptance_ids`, `excluded` with `reason`, `deferred` with an existing FUT ID in `fut`, or draft-only `gap` with `question`. Every origin criterion needs an entry. Each AC that the evolution adds or changes must appear in a covered entry or in `derived` as `{id, reason}` for an obligation added to address a source gap. A covered entry can cite an existing AC that applies to the change. A structural check cannot judge whether the mapping is semantically adequate.
.roclec/model.md:28:For an origin of kind `fut`, import the draft first and record its promotion or duplicate relationship to that change before approval. A deferred criterion must cite an existing FUT. Inspect the change for its origins and coverage. `list changes --origin ID` matches the declared ID across all origin kinds and locators. Qualify IDs with the source system when otherwise ambiguous. Existing schema-2 proposals without these fields remain readable. Approval requires both fields.
.roclec/model.md:50:`.roclec/flow.toml` (`schema = 1`, optional `view`) is project-owned and holds `[roles.NAME]` (`kind` human|agent), `[criteria.CR-NNN]` (`text`) and `[stages.NAME]` for the ten canonical stages: `description`, `ai`, `reason` (required when `ai = false`), `role`, optional `deliverables` (project-relative paths), `session_evidence` (required|optional), `skills` (IDs of registered references with role `skill`, else `FLOW_SKILL_UNREGISTERED`) and `checkpoint = { decider, criteria, on_reject }`. It is agreed as a reference with role `process` for every component; its agreement pins the exact bytes. `--criteria FILE` is a JSON list `[{id, status, reason}]` with status met|not-met|n/a, exactly the criteria of the decision point. Decisions that carry it record `criteria` and `flow` (the SHA-256 of the flow bytes when decided) on `change approve`, `foundation agree`, `checkpoint` and `reject`; the record keeps the evaluation as made and is never re-evaluated against a later flow.
.roclec/model.md:52:A stage checkpoint is a `checkpoint` decision with subject type `stage`: `subject` {type, entity CHG-ID, digest}, `hook` (pre-implement|pre-integrate|handoff), `component`, `outcome` (approved|rejected), `actor`, `reason`, `criteria`, `flow`, and `run` only for pre-integrate. A rejection adds `consequence`, `corrections` and `fut` (only for `defer`); the approval and the rejection are the same record, with no separate rejection record or frozen copy. Its chain is `(CHG, "checkpoint:<component>")`, so each hook decision links to the previous one of that change component. An approval counts only for the current subject digest and after the latest `revise` rejection. Declared hooks without such an approval fail with `CHECKPOINT_REQUIRED`. A handoff rejection accepts only `defer`, which allows removing that member from the planning release. The generated flow view starts with a managed-view header with its SHA-256; do not edit it. Its "Flow learning" section counts records (flow revisions and the process FUTs they address, rejections per stage, findings, ai = false stages, sessions per role and stage), so a new record makes `check` warn `FLOW_VIEW_STALE`. `views --write` runs only on the trunk: on a branch the warning stays until the work is merged and the view is regenerated there. `docs/flow-retro.md` is the consumer's retrospective, seeded once and never overwritten.
.roclec/model.md:62:An agent session is imported with `evidence record --kind agent-session --file META.json --transcript PATH`; Roclec never parses the host's transcript format. META.json contains model_schema, host, host_session_id, actor, role, model, started_at, ended_at and stage, and must not declare kind. host, host_session_id, actor and model are single-line text; role is a built-in role or an agent role declared in `.roclec/flow.toml`; timestamps are UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` with ended_at not before started_at; stage is a flow stage. Scope depends on the stage: foundation requires subject (a registered reference or ADR ID); release requires release {component, version} of a planned release (optional component equal to it); every other stage requires change_id, and component (within the change scope) is required for design, implement, verify, review and integrate and optional otherwise. The original is kept byte for byte under `.roclec/runtime/sessions/EVD-ID/NAME` (local, untracked, owner-only). The record `.roclec/evidence/EVD-ID.json` adds kind=agent-session, id, executed_by_roclec=false, digest and transcript {name, sha256, size, storage, versioned_sha256, redactions}. Optional `[sessions]` in the profile sets `storage` and `quota_bytes` (default 16 MiB). A transcript over the quota is rejected with SESSION_QUOTA_EXCEEDED and nothing is written; it is never truncated. `versioned-redacted` (default) versions `EVD-ID.session` as strict UTF-8 with each `secret_env` value and `redact_patterns` match replaced by `[REDACTED]` and counts the replacements; `versioned-raw` versions an identical copy and `check` warns SESSION_RAW_VERSIONED because it may contain secrets; `local` versions no copy. `check` reports a missing local original as SESSION_RAW_UNAVAILABLE (non-blocking) and an edited original or copy as HASH_MISMATCH. Sessions are not reports: they never cover acceptance criteria, supersede reports or carry findings.
.roclec/model.md:70:release.json is the sole membership authority: component/version/kind/base_tag and changes [{change_id, intent_revision}], with model_schema. Plan membership through the CLI. Final release verification covers all current integrated contracts (or the declared historical correction baseline), not superseded criteria from earlier member proposals. Ready requires actual tests/observations and current adopted review.
