### Application option c: country selector kept in state

The person picks a country and it is stored in browser storage.

- Advantages: simple.
- Disadvantages: the country is not in the URL; reload and sharing depend on stored state.

### Application option d: one build per country

A build-time variable selects the country.

- Advantages: none relevant.
- Disadvantages: violates P1. Rejected.

## Decision

- **Strapi: option A.** A `Country` collection and form-field, plan and terms collections related to it. It is the only option where countries differ in structure without empty placeholders, and adding a country is a content change.
- **Application: option a.** The country code is the first route segment. It keeps one build, survives reloads and makes each country directly testable.
- **Wizard steps:** the steps are content too. A wizard-step collection related to `Country` defines, per country, each step's order, title and type. Step types are a fixed set implemented in code: form step, plan list, summary and payment. Form fields belong to a form step, so a country can split its data across several form steps. Each country has at least one form step, then exactly one plan list, then exactly one summary and payment step as the last step. A new step type needs code and a new decision.
- **Formatting:** currency and number formats come from the `Country` entry (currency code and locale) and are applied with the browser `Intl` API; no formatting code per country.

## Consequences

- Positive: no country branches in code; a new country is added from Strapi plus its seed data; each wizard step queries content by country code; the business team changes the number and order of form steps per country without code.
- Negative: more content types, relations and seed data to maintain; every content request carries the country; navigation, progress indicator and "keep data when going back" must work for any number of steps.
- Risks: an unknown or unpublished country code in the URL must be handled (the behavior is defined in the specs); relations or step sequences misconfigured in Strapi are caught by content validation (P3).

## Compliance verification

- Application code has no conditions on specific country codes; country data comes only from Strapi.
- Every content request filters by the current country.
- Seed data includes Colombia and Chile, and tests exercise content from both countries.

## Relations

- Supersedes: none.
- Related changes: none yet.

Buen punto: los **pasos también son contenido por país**. Así lo incorporé al ADR:

**Cómo funciona**
- Una colección de pasos del wizard, relacionada con `Country`, define por país el orden, el título y el tipo de cada paso.
- Los **tipos de paso son fijos y viven en el código**: formulario, lista de planes y resumen con pago. Cada país elige cuántos pasos de formulario tiene y qué campos van en cada uno. Por ejemplo, Chile podría separar «datos del titular» y «datos del vehículo» en dos pasos y llegar a 4 en total, mientras Colombia queda en 3.
- Un **tipo de paso nuevo**, por ejemplo uno de «inspección», necesita código y un ADR nuevo.

**Reglas de secuencia que propongo** (no las dijiste; revísalas):
1. Al menos un paso de formulario.
2. Exactamente una lista de planes después de los formularios.
3. Exactamente un resumen con pago, como último paso.

Si Strapi tiene una secuencia que no cumple esto, la validación de contenido (P3) lo detecta.

**Otros cambios en el ADR**
- Nuevo driver: el número y el orden de pasos pueden variar por país.
- Nueva consecuencia negativa: la navegación, el indicador de progreso y «mantener datos al volver» deben funcionar con cualquier número de pasos.
- Nueva verificación: ningún número ni orden de pasos fijo en el código.
- **También propuesta mía:** sembrar CO y CL con configuraciones de pasos **distintas**, para demostrar que funciona.

**Coherencia con lo acordado:** `docs/context.md` dice «Any additional step needs a justified decision». Este ADR es esa decisión justificada, así que no lo contradice.

content.text:
Este es un ejemplo **ilustrativo** de cómo quedaría en Strapi 5 según ADR-001. El modelo definitivo, con sus campos exactos, se decide en `architecture` y en los specs.

## Tipos de contenido

```
Country                         WizardStep
├─ code        (uid: co, cl)    ├─ country     → Country (many-to-one)
├─ name        (text)           ├─ order       (integer)
├─ currency    (COP, CLP)       ├─ title       (text)
└─ locale      (es-CO, es-CL)   ├─ type        (enum: form | plans | summary)
                                └─ fields      → FormField (one-to-many, solo si type = form)

FormField                       Plan
├─ step        → WizardStep     ├─ country     → Country
├─ name        (key: documentNumber)   ├─ name, description
├─ label       (text)           ├─ basePrice   (decimal)
├─ type        (enum: text | number | select | date | checkbox)
├─ required    (boolean)        ├─ coverages, benefits (components)
├─ validation  (component: min, max, pattern…)  ├─ order, recommended, active
├─ helpText, errorMessage       └─ (draft & publish)
├─ order       (integer)
└─ options     (component repetible, para select)   Terms
                                                     ├─ country → Country
                                                     └─ text   (rich text)
```

## Datos de ejemplo: Colombia con 3 pasos, Chile con 4

| País | order | title | type | campos |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **co** | 1 | Tus datos y tu vehículo | form | Tipo de documento (select: CC, CE), Número de cédula, Fecha de nacimiento, Placa, Marca (select), Año |
| **co** | 2 | Elige tu plan | plans | — |
| **co** | 3 | Resumen y pago | summary | — |
| **cl** | 1 | Tus datos | form | RUT, Fecha de nacimiento |
| **cl** | 2 | Tu vehículo | form | Patente, Marca (select), Año |
| **cl** | 3 | Elige tu plan | plans | — |
| **cl** | 4 | Resumen y pago | summary | — |

Un campo de ejemplo, el RUT de Chile:

```json
{
  "name": "documentNumber",
  "label": "RUT",
  "type": "text",
  "required": true,
  "validation": { "pattern": "^\\d{7,8}-[\\dkK]$" },
  "helpText": "Sin puntos, con guion. Ej: 12345678-5",
  "errorMessage": "Ingresa un RUT válido",
  "order": 1
}
```

## Cómo lo pide Angular

Al entrar en `/cl/…`, la app consulta los pasos del país, ordenados y con sus campos:

```
GET /api/wizard-steps?filters[country][code][$eq]=cl&sort=order:asc&populate[fields][sort]=order:asc
GET /api/plans?filters[country][code][$eq]=cl&filters[active][$eq]=true&sort=order:asc
GET /api/terms?filters[country][code][$eq]=cl
```

Con la respuesta, el wizard:
- dibuja 4 pasos y su indicador de progreso;
- genera el formulario de cada paso `form` con sus campos;
- muestra los precios en CLP con `Intl.NumberFormat('es-CL', { currency: 'CLP' })`.

Para Colombia, las mismas consultas con `co` devuelven 3 pasos, y no hay ni una línea de código distinta.

**Negocio, desde el panel de Strapi**, puede pasar «Placa» a un paso nuevo, reordenar pasos o despublicar un plan sin desplegar. Si deja una secuencia inválida, por ejemplo sin paso `summary`, la validación de P3 muestra un error controlado.

# ADR-001: Multi-country content strategy

## Context and problem

The product sells car insurance in Colombia and Chile with one application and one build ([context](../context.md), principle P1). Each country has its own identity documents, vehicle identifiers, currency, coverages, plans, terms and copy, and the business team changes them from Strapi without a deployment (P2).

Two things must be decided: how Strapi models content per country, and how the Angular application knows which country it is serving. Without a decision, each user story would solve it differently and the three wizard steps would diverge.

## Decision drivers

- One build serves both countries; no country-specific code branches (P1).
- The business team adds, removes and reorders fields and plans per country from Strapi (P2).
- Countries differ in structure, not only in wording: Colombia uses *cédula* and *placa*, Chile uses RUT and *patente*.
- The number and order of wizard steps can differ by country (for example three steps in Colombia and four in Chile).
- Only published and active content for the current country is shown.
- Prices are shown in the country's currency and format.
- Adding a country later should not require code changes.
- The project starts locally with a single command.

## Considered options

### Strapi option A: `Country` collection with related content

A `Country` collection (code, name, currency, formatting locale). Form fields, plans and terms are their own collections, each entry related to one country.

- Advantages: each country has its own fields, order and required flags; plans and fields are edited and published independently; filtering by country, status and order is a simple query; a new country is a new entry.
- Disadvantages: more collections and relations to model and seed.

### Strapi option B: Strapi i18n locales per country

Locales such as `es-CO` and `es-CL`, with each entry localized per locale.

- Advantages: built into Strapi.
- Disadvantages: i18n localizes the same content into languages, while countries have different fields; it forces empty or "not applicable" entries per country and mixes country with language.

### Strapi option C: one document per country

A single `Country` entry holding fields, plans and terms as components or dynamic zones.

- Advantages: one request per country.
- Disadvantages: a large document; publishing one plan change publishes the whole country; filtering active plans and ordering is harder.

### Application option a: country prefix in the URL

Routes start with the country code (`/co/...`, `/cl/...`); the root lets the person choose a country.

- Advantages: one build; shareable links per country; reload keeps the country; easy to test end to end.
- Disadvantages: the code in the URL must be validated.

### Application option b: subdomain or domain per country

The host (`co.…`, `cl.…`) selects the country.

- Advantages: clean URLs per market.
- Disadvantages: requires DNS or proxy setup; hard to reproduce with a single local command.

### Application option c: country selector kept in state

The person picks a country and it is stored in browser storage.

- Advantages: simple.
- Disadvantages: the country is not in the URL; reload and sharing depend on stored state.

### Application option d: one build per country

A build-time variable selects the country.

- Advantages: none relevant.
- Disadvantages: violates P1. Rejected.

## Decision

- **Strapi: option A.** A `Country` collection and form-field, plan and terms collections related to it. It is the only option where countries differ in structure without empty placeholders, and adding a country is a content change.
- **Application: option a.** The country code is the first route segment. It keeps one build, survives reloads and makes each country directly testable.
- **Wizard steps:** the steps are content too. A wizard-step collection related to `Country` defines, per country, each step's order, title and type. Step types are a fixed set implemented in code: form step, plan list, summary and payment. Form fields belong to a form step, so a country can split its data across several form steps. Each country has at least one form step, then exactly one plan list, then exactly one summary and payment step as the last step. A new step type needs code and a new decision.
- **Formatting:** currency and number formats come from the `Country` entry (currency code and locale) and are applied with the browser `Intl` API; no formatting code per country.

## Consequences

- Positive: no country branches in code; a new country is added from Strapi plus its seed data; each wizard step queries content by country code; the business team changes the number and order of form steps per country without code.
- Negative: more content types, relations and seed data to maintain; every content request carries the country; navigation, progress indicator and "keep data when going back" must work for any number of steps.
- Risks: an unknown or unpublished country code in the URL must be handled (the behavior is defined in the specs); relations or step sequences misconfigured in Strapi are caught by content validation (P3).

## Compliance verification

- Application code has no conditions on specific country codes; country data comes only from Strapi.
- Every content request filters by the current country.
- The wizard's steps come from Strapi; no step count or order is hard-coded.
- Seed data includes Colombia and Chile with different step configurations, and tests exercise content from both countries.

## Relations

## Illustrative model

Not normative: it shows the shape of the decision. The exact content types and fields are defined in the architecture reference and the specs.

### Content types

```
Country                         WizardStep
├─ code        (uid: co, cl)    ├─ country     → Country (many-to-one)
├─ name                         ├─ order
├─ currency    (COP, CLP)       ├─ title
└─ locale      (es-CO, es-CL)   ├─ type        (form | plans | summary)
                                └─ fields      → FormField (only when type = form)

FormField                       Plan                     Terms
├─ step        → WizardStep     ├─ country → Country     ├─ country → Country
├─ name, label                  ├─ name, description     └─ text
├─ type (text | number | select | date | checkbox)
├─ required                     ├─ basePrice
├─ validation (min, max, pattern…)   ├─ coverages, benefits
├─ helpText, errorMessage       ├─ order, recommended, active
├─ order                        └─ draft and publish
└─ options (for select)
```

### Steps per country

| Country | Order | Title | Type | Fields |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| co | 1 | Tus datos y tu vehículo | form | Tipo de documento, Número de cédula, Fecha de nacimiento, Placa, Marca, Año |
| co | 2 | Elige tu plan | plans | — |
| co | 3 | Resumen y pago | summary | — |
| cl | 1 | Tus datos | form | RUT, Fecha de nacimiento |
| cl | 2 | Tu vehículo | form | Patente, Marca, Año |
| cl | 3 | Elige tu plan | plans | — |
| cl | 4 | Resumen y pago | summary | — |

### Requests for `/cl/…`

```
GET /api/wizard-steps?filters[country][code][$eq]=cl&sort=order:asc&populate[fields][sort]=order:asc
GET /api/plans?filters[country][code][$eq]=cl&filters[active][$eq]=true&sort=order:asc
GET /api/terms?filters[country][code][$eq]=cl
```

The same requests with `co` return three steps; the application code is the same.

Sí, conviene dejarlas, por dos razones:

1. **Es la parte que le da valor al ADR.** Sin las alternativas, quien lo lea más adelante (una persona o un agente) no sabe por qué no se usó i18n de Strapi o un subdominio, y puede volver a proponerlo. La sección «Decision» dice qué elegimos; las alternativas dicen qué descartamos y por qué.
2. **La plantilla de Roclec lo pide:** «Describe at least two real options, each as its own `###` subsection».

Lo que sí se puede hacer es **acortarlas**, si te parece largo:
- Quitar la opción **d** (un build por país) como subsección y dejarla en una línea: «A build per country was rejected because it violates P1».
- Reducir cada opción a una línea de ventaja y una de desventaja.

Mi recomendación es dejarlas como están. Si prefieres el ADR más corto, aplico esos dos recortes.

**CR-003: ¿no contradice lo ya acordado?**
- Aplica P1, P2 y P3 de la constitución.
- Usa SQLite, Zod y los tipos generados del stack sin cambiarlos.
- No toca el flujo.

# Architecture How the product is built. It applies [ADR-001](adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md) and the [principles](../.roclec/constitution.md); technologies are in [docs/stack.md](stack.md). ## Overview ```mermaid flowchart LR P["Person (browser)"] --> W["apps/web
Angular SPA"] W -- "read content
(public role, read-only)" --> C["apps/cms
Strapi 5"] W -- "price quote,
simulated payment" --> C C --> D[("SQLite")] S["packages/shared
types and Zod schemas"] -.-> W S -.-> C ``` ## Parts ### `apps/web`: Angular single-page application - **Country resolution:** the first route segment is the country code (`/co/…`, `/cl/…`); the root lets the person choose a country (ADR-001). - **Content client:** reads the country, its wizard steps with their fields, its plans and its terms from Strapi, filtered by country. Every response is validated with the shared Zod schemas before use; invalid or missing content shows a controlled message (P3). - **Wizard shell:** builds the wizard from the country's step configuration. Each step type maps to one component: form step, plan list, summary and payment. Navigation and the progress indicator work for any number of steps; no step count or order is hard-coded. - **Form step:** generated with Angular Signal Forms from the field configuration (type, required flag, validations, help text, error message, order). - **Wizard state:** a signals-based store per country holds the entered data and the chosen plan, mirrored to `sessionStorage`. Data survives going back and reloading the page and is discarded when the tab closes. - **Formatting:** prices and numbers use the country's currency and locale with the `Intl` API. ### `apps/cms`: Strapi 5 with SQLite - **Content types:** `Country`, wizard steps, form fields, plans and terms, related as in ADR-001, with draft and publish. - **Custom endpoints:** - *Price quote:* applies the documented simulated rule to the plan's base price and the entered data and returns the final price. - *Simulated payment:* returns success or failure and, on success, a simulated quote number. - Both are stateless: no quote, payment or personal data is stored (P5). - **Public role:** read-only access (`find`, `findOne`) to the content types the wizard reads, plus the two custom endpoints. Nothing else. No API token reaches the browser (P4). - **Seed data:** Colombia and Chile, with different step configurations. ### `packages/shared` TypeScript types generated from the Strapi content types and the Zod schemas that validate them, used by both applications. ### `e2e` Playwright tests run against the full stack started with Docker Compose. ## Request flow 1. The person opens `/{country}/…`; the application loads the country, its steps, plans and terms and validates them. 2. Each form step stores its valid data in the wizard state; the next step is enabled only when the current one is valid. 3. The plan list shows the country's active, published plans; on selection, the application asks the price endpoint for the final price. 4. The summary shows the entered data, the chosen plan and its final price; after the terms are accepted, the payment endpoint is called once and its result is shown. ## Runtime Docker Compose starts two services with one command: `cms` (Strapi with its SQLite file in a volume and the seed data) and `web` (the built Angular application served as static files). ## Decisions and alternatives | Decision | Chosen | Alternatives considered | | --- | --- | --- | | Wizard state between steps | Signals store mirrored to `sessionStorage` | In memory only (lost on reload); `localStorage` (personal data kept on disk longer) | | Content access without secrets | Browser calls Strapi with a read-only public role | Backend-for-frontend or server-side rendering holding a read token | | Simulated price and payment | Stateless custom endpoints in Strapi | Pure functions and a mock service in the front end | | Rendering | Static single-page application | Server-side rendering with Node |

content.text:
Redacté el borrador [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) con tus 4 decisiones:

- **Estado del wizard:** store con signals, reflejado en `sessionStorage`.
- **Acceso al CMS:** el navegador llama a Strapi con un rol público de solo lectura.
- **Precio y pago simulados:** dos endpoints propios en Strapi.
- **Render:** SPA estática.

**Estructura del documento:**
- Diagrama Mermaid de las piezas: web, cms, shared y SQLite.
- Una sección por pieza: `apps/web`, `apps/cms`, `packages/shared` y `e2e`.
- Flujo de una cotización en 4 pasos, el runtime con Docker Compose y la tabla de decisiones con sus alternativas.

**Qué derivé yo y conviene que revises:**
1. **Endpoints sin estado:** el precio y el pago **no guardan** cotizaciones, pagos ni datos personales. Lo deduje de «no database is required» del contexto y de P5.
2. **Permisos del rol público:** `find`/`findOne` en los tipos que lee el wizard, más acceso a los dos endpoints, y nada más (P4). Elegir endpoints en Strapi obliga a abrir esos dos al rol público.
3. **Cuándo se calcula el precio:** al elegir un plan, la app pide el precio final al endpoint.
4. **Datos de prueba:** Colombia y Chile con configuraciones de pasos distintas, como en ADR-001.
5. **Avance entre pasos:** solo se habilita el siguiente paso si el actual es válido (de US-01).

No incluí detalles que corresponden a engineering o al scaffold: el servidor estático concreto, los puertos ni los nombres de las rutas de los endpoints.

content.text:
Sí, va en este documento, pero solo una parte:

- **architecture** define la estructura del front: qué carpetas y capas hay, qué responsabilidad tiene cada una y **qué puede importar qué**. Esto cuesta cambiarlo después y afecta a todos los cambios.
- **engineering**, o la skill propia, define las convenciones finas: nombres de archivo, sufijos, un componente por archivo, cómo se escriben los tests. Lo veremos en el siguiente documento.

Hay tres formas habituales de organizar el front:

| Opción | Idea | A favor | En contra |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A) Por feature** | `core/`, `features/<feature>/` y `shared/`. Cada feature tiene sus `components/`, `services/` y `models/` | Todo lo de una pantalla está junto. Escala bien y encaja con un cambio por historia | Hay que decidir qué va en `core` y qué en `shared` |
| **B) Por tipo** | `components/`, `services/` y `models/` en la raíz | Muy simple al inicio | Cada historia toca todas las carpetas y las features se mezclan |
| **C) Por feature + componentes contenedor y presentacionales** | Como A, pero cada feature separa los **contenedores**, que inyectan estado y servicios, de los **presentacionales**, que solo reciben inputs y emiten outputs | Los presentacionales se prueban aislados con Angular Testing Library. Las reglas de dependencia son claras | Un poco más de estructura |

**Recomiendo C.**

- **Formatting:** prices and numbers use the country's currency and locale with the `Intl` API.

#### Front-end structure

Organized by feature, with container and presentational components. File naming conventions are defined in the engineering reference.

```
apps/web/src/app/
├─ core/                  # application-wide singletons
│  ├─ country/            # country resolution from the route
│  ├─ content/            # Strapi client and Zod validation
│  └─ wizard-state/       # signals store mirrored to sessionStorage
├─ features/
│  ├─ country-selection/
│  └─ wizard/
│     ├─ shell/           # container: steps, progress, navigation
│     └─ steps/           # one folder per step type
│        ├─ form-step/
│        │  ├─ (container)
│        │  ├─ components/  # presentational, e.g. dynamic field
│        │  ├─ services/
│        │  └─ models/
│        ├─ plan-list/
│        └─ summary/
└─ shared/
   ├─ ui/                 # presentational components based on Spartan UI
   └─ utils/              # pure functions (formatting, masking)
```

- **Containers** inject state and services, and pass data down.
- **Presentational components** receive inputs and emit outputs only; they inject no state or services and are tested in isolation.
- **Dependency rules:** `features` may import `core` and `shared`; `core` may import `shared`; `shared` imports nothing from the application; features do not import each other. Inside `wizard`, the shell selects the step component by step type.
- Content models come from `packages/shared`; feature `models/` hold only view models of that feature.

# Architecture How the product is built. It applies [ADR-001](adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md) and the [principles](../.roclec/constitution.md); technologies are in [docs/stack.md](stack.md). ## Overview ```mermaid flowchart LR P["Person (browser)"] --> W["apps/web
Angular SPA"] W -- "read content
(public role, read-only)" --> C["apps/cms
Strapi 5"] W -- "price quote,
simulated payment" --> C C --> D[("SQLite")] S["packages/shared
types and Zod schemas"] -.-> W S -.-> C ``` ## Parts ### `apps/web`: Angular single-page application - **Country resolution:** the first route segment is the country code (`/co/…`, `/cl/…`); the root lets the person choose a country (ADR-001). - **Content client:** reads the country, its wizard steps with their fields, its plans and its terms from Strapi, filtered by country. Every response is validated with the shared Zod schemas before use; invalid or missing content shows a controlled message (P3). - **Wizard shell:** builds the wizard from the country's step configuration. Each step type maps to one component: form step, plan list, summary and payment. Navigation and the progress indicator work for any number of steps; no step count or order is hard-coded. - **Form step:** generated with Angular Signal Forms from the field configuration (type, required flag, validations, help text, error message, order). - **Wizard state:** a signals-based store per country holds the entered data and the chosen plan, mirrored to `sessionStorage`. Data survives going back and reloading the page and is discarded when the tab closes. - **Formatting:** prices and numbers use the country's currency and locale with the `Intl` API. ### `apps/cms`: Strapi 5 with SQLite - **Content types:** `Country`, wizard steps, form fields, plans and terms, related as in ADR-001, with draft and publish. - **Custom endpoints:** - *Price quote:* applies the documented simulated rule to the plan's base price and the entered data and returns the final price. - *Simulated payment:* returns success or failure and, on success, a simulated quote number. - Both are stateless: no quote, payment or personal data is stored (P5). - **Public role:** read-only access (`find`, `findOne`) to the content types the wizard reads, plus the two custom endpoints. Nothing else. No API token reaches the browser (P4). - **Seed data:** Colombia and Chile, with different step configurations. ### `packages/shared` TypeScript types generated from the Strapi content types and the Zod schemas that validate them, used by both applications. ### `e2e` Playwright tests run against the full stack started with Docker Compose. ## Request flow 1. The person opens `/{country}/…`; the application loads the country, its steps, plans and terms and validates them. 2. Each form step stores its valid data in the wizard state; the next step is enabled only when the current one is valid. 3. The plan list shows the country's active, published plans; on selection, the application asks the price endpoint for the final price. 4. The summary shows the entered data, the chosen plan and its final price; after the terms are accepted, the payment endpoint is called once and its result is shown. ## Runtime Docker Compose starts two services with one command: `cms` (Strapi with its SQLite file in a volume and the seed data) and `web` (the built Angular application served as static files). ## Decisions and alternatives | Decision | Chosen | Alternatives considered | | --- | --- | --- | | Wizard state between steps | Signals store mirrored to `sessionStorage` | In memory only (lost on reload); `localStorage` (personal data kept on disk longer) | | Content access without secrets | Browser calls Strapi with a read-only public role | Backend-for-frontend or server-side rendering holding a read token | | Simulated price and payment | Stateless custom endpoints in Strapi | Pure functions and a mock service in the front end | | Rendering | Static single-page application | Server-side rendering with Node |

Strapi ya trae su propia estructura de carpetas. No hay que inventarla, pero conviene fijar **dónde van las pocas piezas que no son estándar**:

**Lo que Strapi ya impone (no se decide):**
```
apps/cms/
├─ config/                     # server, database (SQLite), plugins
├─ database/migrations/
├─ src/
│  ├─ api/<type>/              # uno por content type: country, wizard-step, form-field, plan, terms
│  │  ├─ content-types/<type>/schema.json
│  │  ├─ controllers/  routes/  services/
│  ├─ components/<category>/   # componentes reutilizables: validation, coverage, option…
│  └─ index.ts                 # register / bootstrap
└─ types/generated/            # tipos generados (van a packages/shared)
```

**Lo que sí conviene decidir:**

| Pieza | Propuesta | Por qué |
|---|---|---|
| Endpoints de precio y pago | Una API **sin content type**, `src/api/quote/`, con sus `routes`, `controllers` y `services` | Es la forma estándar de Strapi para endpoints propios. No crea tablas, así que queda sin estado como pide la arquitectura |
| Regla de precio | Función pura dentro del `service` de `quote` | Se prueba con un test unitario sin levantar Strapi |
| Permisos del rol público | Se aplican **por código** en el `bootstrap`, de forma idempotente | Con `docker compose up` desde cero quedan iguales siempre. Si se configuran a mano en el panel, P4 no es reproducible ni se puede revisar |
| Datos de prueba de CO y CL | Módulo de seed que se ejecuta en el `bootstrap` **solo si la base está vacía** | Cumple «un solo comando con datos de ambos países» sin pisar lo que negocio edite después |

Recomiendo añadir una subsección **«CMS structure»** con esa tabla y el árbol, igual que hicimos con el front.

# Engineering conventions

How code is written in this repository. It applies the [principles](../.roclec/constitution.md), [ADR-001](adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md) and the [architecture](architecture.md); technologies are in [docs/stack.md](stack.md). Testing is defined in the verification reference.

## Language

- Code, identifiers, comments, commits and documentation are in English.
- User-facing copy is in Spanish and comes from Strapi. The only copy written in the front end is the fallback shown when content cannot be loaded or is invalid, also in Spanish.

## TypeScript

- Strict mode in every package; no `any`.
- Data crossing a boundary (Strapi responses, browser storage, route parameters) is typed `unknown` until a Zod schema from `packages/shared` validates it (P3).
- Content types come from `packages/shared`; they are not redefined in the applications.

## Angular (`apps/web`)

- Standalone components, signals, `input()`, `output()` and `inject()`; built-in control flow (`@if`, `@for`); no NgModules.
- `OnPush` change detection in every component.
- File names follow the Angular style guide (v20 and later): kebab-case without type suffixes, for example `plan-card.ts`, `wizard-state.ts`. The folder tells the role: containers sit at the root of their feature folder and presentational components under `components/` (architecture).
- Data that is loaded asynchronously uses `httpResource` or `resource`. Every view that loads data handles its loading, error and empty states explicitly.
- Form steps use Signal Forms built from the field configuration; validators and error messages come from Strapi.
- Only the wizard-state store reads and writes `sessionStorage`; components use the store's API.
- No component contains conditions on specific country codes or a fixed number of steps (ADR-001).
- UI is built from Spartan UI components and Tailwind CSS utilities.

## Strapi (`apps/cms`)

- TypeScript.
- Content-type schemas live in the repository (`schema.json`); changes made with the admin Content-Type Builder during development are committed.
- Controllers stay thin; logic lives in services. The simulated price rule is a pure function in the `quote` service.
- Public role permissions and seed data are applied in the bootstrap and are idempotent (architecture).

## Security

- No API token reaches the browser; the front end reads content only through the read-only public role (P4).
- Secrets come from environment variables. `.env` files are never committed; `.env.example` lists every variable without values.
- Strapi's CORS allows only the web application's origin.
- The public role has only the permissions listed in the architecture; adding one requires updating that reference.
- Personal data entered in the wizard is not logged.

## Quality

- ESLint (angular-eslint) and Prettier pass in every package before a change is integrated.

## Commits

- Conventional Commits in English.
- Commits created by an AI agent end with a `Co-Authored-By` trailer that names the model.

# Technology stack

## Choices

| Area | Choice | Location | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Front end | Angular 21 or later | `apps/web/` | Standalone components, signals and built-in control flow (`@if`, `@for`); no NgModules |
| Content backend | Strapi 5 or later | `apps/cms/` | Holds the form fields and plans per country |
| CMS database | SQLite | `apps/cms/` | Used only by Strapi; quote data stays in the front end |
| CMS types | TypeScript types generated from the Strapi content types | `apps/cms/types/` | The front end uses them instead of hand-written copies |
| UI components | Spartan UI | `apps/web/` | — |
| Styling | Tailwind CSS | `apps/web/` | — |
| Forms | Angular Signal Forms | `apps/web/` | The step 1 form is generated dynamically from the Strapi configuration, with typed validations |
| Runtime validation | Zod | `apps/web/` | Validates the content returned by Strapi before the application uses it |
| Unit tests | Vitest (Vite) with Angular Testing Library | `apps/web/` | — |
| End-to-end tests | Playwright | `e2e/` | — |
| Accessibility tests | @axe-core/playwright | `e2e/` | Runs inside the end-to-end tests |
| Lint and format | ESLint (angular-eslint) and Prettier | each package | — |
| Runtime | Node.js 26.13.1 | all packages | — |
| Local environment | Docker Compose | `docker-compose.yml` | The whole project starts with a single command (`docker compose up`), with seed data for both countries |
| Package manager | npm workspaces | root `package.json` | One lockfile at the root; workspaces `apps/web`, `apps/cms`, `e2e` and `packages/shared`. Scripts are run with `npm run` |
| Shared code | Workspace package | `packages/shared/` | Types and Zod schemas used by both the front end and the CMS |

## Covered by other references

- Multi-country content strategy: ADR-001.
- Security (Strapi tokens, public role permissions): engineering reference.
- Testing scope (unit and end-to-end): verification reference.
- Accessibility and responsive behavior: design reference.

En **`docs/engineering.md`**. SOLID y clean code son convenciones de cómo se escribe el código, no principios del producto. La constitución recoge reglas del negocio que no se negocian, como un solo build o nada de secretos en el navegador; llevarlos allí mezclaría niveles.

Te recomiendo **no dejarlo como «follow SOLID and clean code»**, porque así nadie puede revisarlo. Mejor una sección **«Design and clean code»** con reglas concretas que un revisor pueda comprobar:

| Principio | Regla concreta en este proyecto |
|---|---|
| **S**ingle responsibility | Un componente, servicio o función hace una sola cosa; los contenedores orquestan y los presentacionales solo muestran |
| **O**pen/closed | Un tipo de paso o de campo nuevo se añade con un componente nuevo registrado por tipo, sin modificar el shell ni los `switch` existentes |
| **L**iskov | Todos los componentes de paso cumplen el mismo contrato de entradas y salidas, así el shell los trata igual |
| **I**nterface segregation | Los servicios exponen interfaces pequeñas por uso: lectura de contenido, precio, pago |
| **D**ependency inversion | Las features dependen de abstracciones inyectadas (`InjectionToken`) para contenido, precio y pago, no de clientes HTTP concretos. Así se sustituyen en los tests |
| Clean code | Nombres que dicen la intención; funciones cortas; sin números ni strings mágicos; sin código comentado ni muerto; reglas de negocio como funciones puras; sin duplicar lógica |

El **commit del stack** sigue pendiente. Puedo hacerlo ahora y luego añadir esta sección al borrador de engineering, o al revés.

## Design and clean code

SOLID and clean code, stated as rules a reviewer can check:

- **Single responsibility:** a component, service or function does one thing. Containers orchestrate; presentational components only display.
- **Open/closed:** a new step type or field type is added as a new component registered by type, without editing the wizard shell or existing switches.
- **Liskov substitution:** every step component honors the same input and output contract, so the shell treats them alike.
- **Interface segregation:** services expose small, use-specific interfaces: content reading, price quote, payment.
- **Dependency inversion:** features depend on injected abstractions (`InjectionToken`) for content, price and payment, not on concrete HTTP clients, so tests can replace them.
- **Clean code:** names state intent; functions are short; no magic numbers or strings; no commented-out or dead code; business rules are pure functions; logic is not duplicated.

# Engineering conventions

How code is written in this repository. It applies the [principles](../.roclec/constitution.md), [ADR-001](adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md) and the [architecture](architecture.md); technologies are in [docs/stack.md](stack.md). Testing is defined in the verification reference.

## Language

- Code, identifiers, comments, commits and documentation are in English.
- User-facing copy is in Spanish and comes from Strapi. The only copy written in the front end is the fallback shown when content cannot be loaded or is invalid, also in Spanish.

## TypeScript

- Strict mode in every package; no `any`.
- Data crossing a boundary (Strapi responses, browser storage, route parameters) is typed `unknown` until a Zod schema from `packages/shared` validates it (P3).
- Content types come from `packages/shared`; they are not redefined in the applications.

## Angular (`apps/web`)

- Standalone components, signals, `input()`, `output()` and `inject()`; built-in control flow (`@if`, `@for`); no NgModules.
- `OnPush` change detection in every component.
- File names follow the Angular style guide (v20 and later): kebab-case without type suffixes, for example `plan-card.ts`, `wizard-state.ts`. The folder tells the role: containers sit at the root of their feature folder and presentational components under `components/` (architecture).
- Data that is loaded asynchronously uses `httpResource` or `resource`. Every view that loads data handles its loading, error and empty states explicitly.
- Form steps use Signal Forms built from the field configuration; validators and error messages come from Strapi.
- Only the wizard-state store reads and writes `sessionStorage`; components use the store's API.
- No component contains conditions on specific country codes or a fixed number of steps (ADR-001).
- UI is built from Spartan UI components and Tailwind CSS utilities.

## Strapi (`apps/cms`)

- TypeScript.
- Content-type schemas live in the repository (`schema.json`); changes made with the admin Content-Type Builder during development are committed.
- Controllers stay thin; logic lives in services. The simulated price rule is a pure function in the `quote` service.
- Public role permissions and seed data are applied in the bootstrap and are idempotent (architecture).

## Security

- No API token reaches the browser; the front end reads content only through the read-only public role (P4).
- Secrets come from environment variables. `.env` files are never committed; `.env.example` lists every variable without values.
- Strapi's CORS allows only the web application's origin.
- The public role has only the permissions listed in the architecture; adding one requires updating that reference.
- Personal data entered in the wizard is not logged.

## Quality

- ESLint (angular-eslint) and Prettier pass in every package before a change is integrated.

## Commits

- Conventional Commits in English.
- Commits created by an AI agent end with a `Co-Authored-By` trailer that names the model.

Anoté tus 4 decisiones: e2e de ambos países, umbral de cobertura solo para la lógica pura, e2e como check de `run verify` y Vitest también en cms y shared.

La cuarta decisión obliga a cambiar el stack. Al revisarlo encontré **dos filas que ya no encajan con lo acordado después**, y las corregí en el mismo cambio:

| Fila | Antes | Ahora | Motivo |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit tests | Vitest + ATL en `apps/web/` | Vitest en `apps/web/`, `apps/cms/` y `packages/shared/`; Angular Testing Library para componentes | Tu decisión 4 |
| Forms | «The **step 1** form is generated…» | «**Form steps** are generated…» | ADR-001 permite varios pasos de formulario por país |
| Runtime validation | Zod en `apps/web/` | Zod en `packages/shared/`, usado por `apps/web/` | La arquitectura pone los esquemas en `packages/shared` |

`stack` queda **stale** hasta que lo vuelvas a acordar (nuevo SHA-256 `732c6683…49e2f`).

- **CR-001:** la fila de unit tests es tu decisión. Las otras dos correcciones las propuse yo, para alinearlo con ADR-001 y la arquitectura. Si no las quieres, márcalo y las revierto.
- **CR-002 y CR-003:** el stack queda coherente con ADR-001 y con la arquitectura, y deja de contradecirlos.

Después redacto `docs/verification.md`.

input.content:
# Verification

How the product is verified. It applies the [principles](../.roclec/constitution.md), [ADR-001](adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md), the [architecture](architecture.md) and the [engineering conventions](engineering.md); tools are in [docs/stack.md](stack.md).

## Test levels

| Level | Tool | What it covers | Location |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | Vitest | Pure functions (formatting, masking, simulated price rule), the wizard-state store, mapping of Strapi validations to form validators, Zod schemas with valid and invalid content | `apps/web/`, `apps/cms/` (`quote` service), `packages/shared/` |
| Component | Vitest with Angular Testing Library | Presentational components in isolation; containers with their injected abstractions replaced; loading, error and empty states | `apps/web/` |
| End-to-end | Playwright | The full flow, from country selection to payment confirmation, for Colombia and for Chile, against the stack started with Docker Compose and its seed data | `e2e/` |
| Accessibility | @axe-core/playwright | An automated scan of every wizard step inside the end-to-end tests | `e2e/` |

## Countries and data

- Tests exercise content from both countries; the seed data gives Colombia and Chile different step configurations, and the end-to-end tests run the flow for each (ADR-001).
- Unit and component tests use fixtures for both countries.
- Only fictitious data is used (P5).

## Traceability

- Every acceptance criterion names how it is verified: unit test, end-to-end test or declared manual check.
- Automated tests include the acceptance criterion ID in their title, for example `AC-03 shows only the active plans of the country`.

input.content:
# Design

How the interface looks and behaves. It makes principle P6 concrete and applies the [principles](../.roclec/constitution.md), [ADR-001](adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md), the [architecture](architecture.md) and the [engineering conventions](engineering.md); UI technologies are in [docs/stack.md](stack.md).

## Accessibility

The target is WCAG 2.2 level AA. In this product that means:

- The whole wizard can be completed with the keyboard only, in a logical tab order and without keyboard traps.
- Focus is always visible and never hidden behind other content.
- Every field has a programmatic label. Help text and error messages are associated with their field.
- When a step cannot advance, focus moves to the first invalid field and the error is announced.
- When the step changes, focus moves to the new step's heading; the progress indicator marks the current step.
- Loading, error and empty states are announced to assistive technologies.
- Color is never the only way to convey meaning: the recommended plan, the selected plan and errors also have text or an icon with a label.
- Text and interface elements meet AA contrast; interactive targets are at least 24 × 24 CSS pixels.
- Motion respects the person's reduced-motion preference.

## Responsive design

- Mobile-first. Reference widths: 375 px (mobile) and 1280 px (desktop).
- Content reflows down to 320 px wide without horizontal scrolling.
- The wizard, the plan list and the summary work at both reference widths with the same content.

## Visual identity per country

- Each country has its own theme, configured in Strapi on its `Country` entry: primary color, accent color and logo.
- The application applies the theme at runtime as CSS custom properties consumed by the Tailwind and Spartan UI tokens. Layout, components and typography are shared by both countries (ADR-001, P1).
- Theme colors must meet AA contrast with the text placed on them. A missing or invalid theme falls back to a default theme (P3).

## Components and styling

- Spartan UI components are used first; layouts and spacing use Tailwind utilities.
- Colors, spacing and typography come from design tokens (CSS custom properties); no hard-coded colors and no inline styles.
- The recommended plan (US-02) is distinguished with a visible text label in addition to its styling.

## Copy

User-facing copy is in Spanish and comes from Strapi; only the fallback for unavailable content lives in the front end (engineering).

## Design skills

During the design stage (UX specification and prototypes) and when reviewing user interface changes, agents use these skills pinned in `skills-lock.json`:

| Skill | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `ui-ux-pro-max` | Interaction patterns for forms, wizards, plan comparison and states |
| `design-lab` | Alternative prototype variations to compare before choosing one |
| `impeccable` | Critique and polish of the chosen design |
| `web-design-guidelines` | Audit against web interface and accessibility guidelines |

The other pinned skills (`design-taste-frontend`, `frontend-design`) target public marketing pages and are not used for the wizard.

## Verification

Automated accessibility scans run inside the end-to-end tests (verification reference). Keyboard-only completion and the reference widths are checked in every prototype review and user interface review.

It makes principle P6 concrete and applies the [principles](../.roclec/constitution.md), [ADR-001](adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md), the [architecture](architecture.md) and the [engineering conventions](engineering.md); UI technologies are in [docs/stack.md](stack.md).

## Accessibility

The target is WCAG 2.2 level AA. In this product that means:

- The whole wizard can be completed with the keyboard only, in a logical tab order and without keyboard traps.
- Focus is always visible and never hidden behind other content.
- Every field has a programmatic label. Help text and error messages are associated with their field.
- When a step cannot advance, focus moves to the first invalid field and the error is announced.
- When the step changes, focus moves to the new step's heading; the progress indicator marks the current step.
- Loading, error and empty states are announced to assistive technologies.
- Color is never the only way to convey meaning: the recommended plan, the selected plan and errors also have text or an icon with a label.
- Text and interface elements meet AA contrast; interactive targets are at least 24 × 24 CSS pixels.
- Motion respects the person's reduced-motion preference.

## Responsive design

- Mobile-first. Reference widths: 375 px (mobile) and 1280 px (desktop).
- Content reflows down to 320 px wide without horizontal scrolling.
- The wizard, the plan list and the summary work at both reference widths with the same content.

## Visual identity per country

- Each country has its own theme, configured in Strapi on its `Country` entry: primary color, accent color and logo.
- The application applies the theme at runtime as CSS custom properties consumed by the Tailwind and Spartan UI tokens. Layout, components and typography are shared by both countries (ADR-001, P1).
- Theme colors must meet AA contrast with the text placed on them. A missing or invalid theme falls back to a default theme (P3).

## Components and styling

- Spartan UI components are used first; layouts and spacing use Tailwind utilities.
- Colors, spacing and typography come from design tokens (CSS custom properties); no hard-coded colors and no inline styles.
- The recommended plan (US-02) is distinguished with a visible text label in addition to its styling.

## Copy

User-facing copy is in Spanish and comes from Strapi; only the fallback for unavailable content lives in the front end (engineering).

## Design skills

During the design stage (UX specification and prototypes) and when reviewing user interface changes, agents use these skills pinned in `skills-lock.json`:

| Skill | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `ui-ux-pro-max` | Interaction patterns for forms, wizards, plan comparison and states |
| `design-lab` | Alternative prototype variations to compare before choosing one |
| `impeccable` | Critique and polish of the chosen design |
| `web-design-guidelines` | Audit against web interface and accessibility guidelines |

The other pinned skills (`design-taste-frontend`, `frontend-design`) target public marketing pages and are not used for the wizard.

## Verification

Automated accessibility scans run inside the end-to-end tests (verification reference). Keyboard-only completion and the reference widths are checked in every prototype review and user interface review.

Redacté el borrador [docs/design.md](docs/design.md).

**Lo que decidiste:**
- WCAG 2.2 AA.
- Tema distinto por país.
- Anchos de referencia de 375 y 1280 px, diseño mobile-first.
- Las 4 skills de diseño: ui-ux-pro-max, design-lab, impeccable y web-design-guidelines. Cada una tiene su uso descrito, y dejé escrito por qué no se usan las otras dos.

**Lo que concreté yo y conviene que revises:**
1. **Reglas de WCAG 2.2 AA aplicadas al wizard:**
   - Al cambiar de paso, el foco va al título.
   - Si no se puede avanzar, el foco va al primer campo inválido.
   - Los estados de carga y error se anuncian.
   - Ningún significado depende solo del color.
   - Objetivos táctiles de al menos 24 × 24 px.
   - Se respeta «reduced motion».
   - El contenido se adapta hasta 320 px de ancho sin scroll horizontal.
2. **Tema por país:**
   - Campos: color primario, color de acento y logo, guardados en `Country`.
   - Se aplica con CSS custom properties sobre los tokens de Tailwind y Spartan. El layout y los componentes son comunes a todos los países.
   - **Los colores deben cumplir el contraste AA.** Si el tema falta o no es válido, se usa un tema por defecto (P3). Sin esto, negocio podría romper la accesibilidad desde Strapi.
3. **Estilos:** sin colores fijos en el código ni estilos inline; todo sale de tokens.
4. **Verificación:** en cada revisión de prototipo y de UI se comprueba que el wizard se completa solo con teclado y que funciona en los anchos de referencia.

**Impacto en lo ya acordado:** el tema por país añade campos a `Country`. No contradice ADR-001 ni la arquitectura, porque el modelo del ADR es solo ilustrativo, pero lo amplía. Si quieres, más adelante actualizo el modelo ilustrativo del ADR para que lo refleje. Eso exigiría volver a acordarlo.

content.text:
Respondo primero a las dos preguntas. No he cambiado nada.

## 1. ¿Dónde va el sistema de diseño?

Hoy no hay un archivo específico, y Roclec no lo exige. El rol `design` solo pide **un** documento acordado, que sería `docs/design.md`. Hay dos niveles:

| Nivel | Qué contiene | Dónde lo pondría |
|---|---|---|
| **Especificación** del sistema de diseño | Tokens con nombre y valor (colores semánticos, tipografía, espaciado, radios, sombras), componentes base y sus estados, y la relación entre tokens y tema por país | Una sección **«Design system»** dentro de `docs/design.md`, para que todo quede en una sola referencia acordada. Si crece mucho, puede ir aparte en `docs/design-system.md` y registrarse como otra referencia |
| **Implementación** | Archivo de tokens CSS (`--color-primary`…), configuración del tema de Tailwind y de Spartan | En código, en `apps/web/src/styles/`, al crear el scaffold. No es documentación, y se verifica con los checks |

Recomiendo añadirlo como sección de `docs/design.md` antes de acordarlo.

## 2. ¿Hay problema en usar los sitios de SURA como referencia?

**Como inspiración de patrones, no. Como fuente de identidad visual, sí.**

**Problemas si se copia la identidad:**
- **Marca y derechos:** SURA es una aseguradora real que opera justo en Colombia y Chile. Su nombre, logo, colores corporativos, tipografías propias, imágenes y textos están protegidos por marca o derechos de autor.
- **Suplantación:** este producto pide datos personales y un pago, aunque sean simulados. Si se parece visualmente a SURA, alguien podría tomarlo por un sitio suyo, que es el patrón típico del phishing. Choca además con el espíritu de P5 (todo ficticio).
- **Coherencia con lo acordado:** el tema por país se configura en Strapi. Los temas sembrados no deben ser los de SURA.

**Lo que sí se puede tomar** (son patrones del sector, no propiedad de nadie):
- La estructura del cotizador: pasos, orden de los datos, cómo se presenta el progreso.
- Cómo se comparan los planes: tarjetas, coberturas y el plan recomendado destacado.
- La jerarquía de la información: precio, moneda, letra pequeña y términos.
- Las señales de confianza y el tono del texto, redactados con palabras propias.
- Los patrones de error y ayuda en los campos de documento (cédula, RUT, placa, patente).

**Cómo lo haría:**
1. Analizar ambos sitios **solo para extraer patrones**: navegación del cotizador, formularios, comparación de planes y accesibilidad. Anotarlos sin capturas ni textos copiados.
2. Definir una **marca ficticia propia**, con nombre, logo y paleta propios, y un tema distinto por país que cumpla AA.
3. En `docs/design.md`, citar los sitios como «referencias de patrones de UX del sector» y añadir la regla explícita: **no se usan nombre, logo, colores, tipografías, imágenes ni textos de aseguradoras reales**.

Si te parece, el siguiente paso sería analizar los dos sitios con ese enfoque y traerte los patrones. Con eso redactamos la sección «Design system» y la regla de marca.

# Built-in browser

The built-in browser is a real browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, separate from the person's Chrome. Its tools are named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*` when the session itself runs inside the desktop app, and `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when the session runs in the cloud (started from the web, a phone, or the desktop app) and is linked to the person's computer. The names after the prefix are the same either way, Claude uses whichever prefix is actually present, and this skill refers to the tools by the part after the prefix.

If the only built-in browser tool present is `enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser`, Claude calls it first: it turns the built-in browser on for this conversation, and the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` tools appear once it has run.

## What the person can see

The browser pane shares the desktop app's side panel with artifacts, documents, and file previews, and the panel shows one of them at a time. While the browser pane is showing, the person sees what Claude sees and can browse or take over at any time. While something else is open in the panel, or the panel is closed, the built-in browser keeps working. Claude does not tell the person that they missed it or could not see it, because Claude cannot tell what they were watching.

Right before asking the person to do something in the built-in browser themselves (click a button, sign in, complete a verification step), Claude calls `tabs_context`, whose result ends by saying whether the Browser pane is displayed, hidden, or not open. If the pane is not open, Claude opens the page first and checks again. If the pane is hidden, Claude first asks the person to bring the browser back in the Claude desktop app: press Cmd+Shift+B on Mac or Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows, or close whatever else is open in the side panel and click the globe icon (the Browser button). When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, Claude usually cannot tell whether the person is reading this conversation in the desktop app, on the claude.ai website or on a phone, and the shortcut and the globe icon work only in the desktop app, so before those steps Claude says that if they are not in the Claude desktop app on the computer whose browser Claude is using, they need to open this conversation there first. Claude then says what to do in the browser. Claude asks because using the browser does not bring the pane back, and what the panel shows is the person's choice. Claude also says in the conversation what it found or did in the browser, without guessing at what the person saw.

## Sign-ins persist, and they are the person's

The built-in browser keeps its own persistent profile, shared across the desktop app's sessions. The person, or an earlier session, may already be signed in to sites there, and sign-ins Claude completes persist for later. Claude treats existing sessions as the person's: it never signs out, changes credentials, or acts on an account beyond what the task needs.

## Tabs

The built-in browser has tabs. `preview_start` with a `url` opens an additional tab at that URL in one call and returns a `tabId`, leaving existing tabs untouched, so Claude prefers it over `tabs_create` followed by `navigate` when the destination is already known. `navigate`, `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, `computer`, `form_input`, and the console and network readers act on the tab named by `tabId`; omitting `tabId` targets the active tab, and `tabs_context` lists the open tabs.

## Loading via ToolSearch

Claude loads the built-in browser tools in bulk, not one-by-one: if they are in the deferred list, Claude loads them all in a single ToolSearch call whose query is their full name prefix, for example `{ query: "mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__", max_results: 64 }`.

## Reading pages

Claude prefers `get_page_text` and `read_page` over screenshots for reading, because they return the page's actual text and structure rather than pixels of the visible viewport. `computer` with action "screenshot" is for when the visual layout is the point or the person asks to see the page.

## Site approvals, blocked sites, and request_access

Depending on the person's approval settings, the person may be asked to approve a site before Claude acts on it, and some sites are blocked outright. Claude waits for a pending approval rather than working around it. If a page is refused or an approval is declined, Claude tells the person and moves on rather than retrying.

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, approvals can be answered from any of the person's devices and may take a moment to arrive, and the session may also have a `request_access` tool. If a browser tool answers that the site is not allowed yet and `request_access` is present, Claude calls it with that site's URL and scope "once" (or "site" when the task will keep using that site), waits for the person's answer, and then retries the original tool. Without `request_access`, a refused site is handled as above: Claude tells the person and moves on.

## What the built-in browser cannot open

The built-in browser cannot open `file://` URLs or `localhost` servers that Claude starts itself, because those run where Claude's shell runs, which is not where the browser pane runs. To show the person HTML that Claude generated, Claude uses an artifact instead.

## When the built-in browser cannot be reached

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, the pane runs in the Claude desktop app on the person's computer while Claude runs elsewhere, so it is reachable only while that app is open and online. If those tool calls cannot reach the desktop app (connection errors or no response), Claude tells the person the built-in browser looks offline on their computer rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

Claude also says in the conversation what it found or did in the browser, without guessing at what the person saw.

## Sign-ins persist, and they are the person's

The built-in browser keeps its own persistent profile, shared across the desktop app's sessions. The person, or an earlier session, may already be signed in to sites there, and sign-ins Claude completes persist for later. Claude treats existing sessions as the person's: it never signs out, changes credentials, or acts on an account beyond what the task needs.

## Tabs

The built-in browser has tabs. `preview_start` with a `url` opens an additional tab at that URL in one call and returns a `tabId`, leaving existing tabs untouched, so Claude prefers it over `tabs_create` followed by `navigate` when the destination is already known. `navigate`, `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, `computer`, `form_input`, and the console and network readers act on the tab named by `tabId`; omitting `tabId` targets the active tab, and `tabs_context` lists the open tabs.

## Loading via ToolSearch

Claude loads the built-in browser tools in bulk, not one-by-one: if they are in the deferred list, Claude loads them all in a single ToolSearch call whose query is their full name prefix, for example `{ query: "mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__", max_results: 64 }`.

## Reading pages

Claude prefers `get_page_text` and `read_page` over screenshots for reading, because they return the page's actual text and structure rather than pixels of the visible viewport. `computer` with action "screenshot" is for when the visual layout is the point or the person asks to see the page.

## Site approvals, blocked sites, and request_access

Depending on the person's approval settings, the person may be asked to approve a site before Claude acts on it, and some sites are blocked outright. Claude waits for a pending approval rather than working around it. If a page is refused or an approval is declined, Claude tells the person and moves on rather than retrying.

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, approvals can be answered from any of the person's devices and may take a moment to arrive, and the session may also have a `request_access` tool. If a browser tool answers that the site is not allowed yet and `request_access` is present, Claude calls it with that site's URL and scope "once" (or "site" when the task will keep using that site), waits for the person's answer, and then retries the original tool. Without `request_access`, a refused site is handled as above: Claude tells the person and moves on.

## What the built-in browser cannot open

The built-in browser cannot open `file://` URLs or `localhost` servers that Claude starts itself, because those run where Claude's shell runs, which is not where the browser pane runs. To show the person HTML that Claude generated, Claude uses an artifact instead.

## When the built-in browser cannot be reached

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, the pane runs in the Claude desktop app on the person's computer while Claude runs elsewhere, so it is reachable only while that app is open and online. If those tool calls cannot reach the desktop app (connection errors or no response), Claude tells the person the built-in browser looks offline on their computer rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

Analicé seguros.sura.cl (home, Seguro Auto Full Cobertura y su formulario de cotización) y sura.co/seguros (home y Seguro de carro digital). Leí estilos y variables CSS desde el navegador. No escribí ni envié nada en los formularios y no cambié ningún archivo.

## Lo que comparten ambos países

Es una sola identidad. Colombia la tiene expuesta como variables CSS, y Chile usa los mismos valores.

| Token | Valor | Uso observado |
|---|---|---|
| Primario | `#2D6DF6` | Header, botones secundarios, labels, enlaces |
| Navy | `#0033A0` | Texto sobre el CTA, barra de navegación, valores de campos |
| Amarillo CTA | `#E3E829` | Botón principal («Cotizar», «Iniciar sesión») |
| Indigo | `#26328C` | Texto de CTA y hover de botones |
| Turquesa | `#00AEC7` | Acento secundario |
| Texto | `#1C1C24` | Cuerpo |
| Gris | `#888B8D` / `#B4B4B5` | Bordes y deshabilitado |
| Alerta | `#DB1A40` | Errores |
| Fondos suaves | `#DFEAFF`, `#F9FAE1`, `#F8F8F8` | Secciones y badges |
| Tipografía | **SuraSans** (Regular, Seminegrita, Negrita) | Toda la UI. Cuerpo de 16 px, títulos de 24 a 48 px |
| Radios | 8, 12, 16, 24 px; botones de 28 a 40 px (píldora) | Campos e tarjetas de 12 px |

## Patrones del cotizador

- **Formulario:** label arriba en azul, de 14 px y con `*` si es obligatorio. Campo de 48 px de alto, radio de 12 px y borde de 1 px. Placeholder con ejemplo (`Ej: ABC123`, `12345678`).
- **Opciones cortas:** botones segmentados «Sí / No» y tarjetas de radio («Carro particular / Transporte público»).
- **CTA principal:** píldora amarilla con texto navy, **gris y deshabilitada** hasta que el formulario es válido. Encima, un texto de expectativa («Verás 3 planes con tu precio en segundos»); debajo, un enlace a términos y condiciones.
- **Chile:** el RUT va en dos campos (número y dígito verificador).
- **Planes:** 3 tarjetas en fila con un badge arriba («Más económico», «**Más elegido**», «Más coberturas»). El plan recomendado lleva **borde y fondo azul claro más un badge de texto**, así que no depende solo del color, como pide nuestra regla. Cada tarjeta muestra nombre, subtítulo, botón y coberturas en lista con montos destacados.
- **Accesibilidad:** ambos sitios tienen un panel propio (contraste+, modo oscuro, agrandar texto, espaciado).

## Contraste WCAG AA

| Combinación | Ratio | AA |
|---|---|---|
| Navy sobre amarillo (CTA) | 8.0 | ✅ |
| Blanco sobre azul primario | 4.54 | ✅ (justo) |
| Azul primario como texto o label sobre blanco | 4.54 | ✅ (justo) |
| Alerta sobre blanco | 4.96 | ✅ |
| Gris deshabilitado sobre blanco | 3.59 | ⚠️ AA lo permite en elementos deshabilitados, pero no en texto normal |
| **Amarillo como texto sobre azul** (lo usa el hero de Chile) | 3.42 | ❌ solo vale para texto grande (≥ 24 px, o ≥ 18,7 px en negrita) |

## Qué propongo añadir a `docs/design.md`

1. **Sección «Design system»** con esos tokens como **tema por defecto**. Además, el tema que se siembra en Strapi para CO y CL usaría esta misma paleta, que es la identidad común.
2. **Regla de contraste:** el amarillo solo como fondo de CTA o en texto grande; nunca como texto pequeño sobre azul.
3. **Componentes:** campos de 48 px y radio 12, segmentados y tarjetas de radio, CTA deshabilitado hasta que todo sea válido y tarjetas de plan con badge de texto.
4. **Tipografía:** SuraSans es una fuente propietaria y no tenemos sus archivos. Usaríamos `SuraSans` si está disponible, con un respaldo abierto de forma parecida (por ejemplo `Nunito Sans`) y `sans-serif`. Lo mismo con el logo: un placeholder hasta tener el oficial.
5. Citar ambos sitios como fuente de la identidad y de los patrones.

Con tema por país y la misma identidad en los dos sitios, los dos temas sembrados serían iguales. El mecanismo queda listo por si algún día difieren.

## Visual identity per country

- Each country has its own theme, configured in Strapi on its `Country` entry: primary color, accent color and logo.
- The application applies the theme at runtime as CSS custom properties consumed by the Tailwind and Spartan UI tokens. Layout, components and typography are shared by both countries (ADR-001, P1).
- Theme colors must meet AA contrast with the text placed on them. A missing or invalid theme falls back to the default theme (P3).
- The seeded themes for Colombia and Chile use the SURA identity below, which today is the same in both countries.

## Design system

The identity and patterns follow SURA's public insurance sites for [Chile](https://seguros.sura.cl/) and [Colombia](https://www.sura.co/seguros).

### Color tokens

| Token | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `primary` | `#2D6DF6` | Header, secondary buttons, field labels, links |
| `primary-strong` | `#0033A0` | Navigation bar, text on the call to action, field values |
| `cta` | `#E3E829` | Background of the primary call to action |
| `cta-foreground` | `#26328C` | Text on the call to action |
| `accent` | `#00AEC7` | Secondary accent |
| `foreground` | `#1C1C24` | Body text |
| `muted` | `#888B8D` | Secondary text |
| `border` | `#B4B4B5` | Field and card borders |
| `disabled` | `#878789` | Disabled controls |
| `danger` | `#DB1A40` | Errors |
| `surface-info` | `#DFEAFF` | Highlighted sections, recommended plan background |
| `surface-cta` | `#F9FAE1` | Soft call-to-action sections |
| `surface-muted` | `#F8F8F8` | Neutral sections |

Contrast rules: `cta` is used only as a background with `cta-foreground` or `primary-strong` text (8:1), never as text on `primary` (3.4:1, below AA for normal text). White on `primary` and `primary` text on white are at the AA limit (4.5:1) and are not lightened.

### Typography

- Font family: `SuraSans` (regular, semibold, bold) when its files are available; otherwise an open fallback of similar shape (`Nunito Sans`), then `sans-serif`.
- Body 16 px; labels and helper text 14 px; headings 24 to 48 px in bold.

### Shape

- Radii: 8, 12, 16 and 24 px; fields and cards use 12 px; buttons are pills (28 px or more).
- Fields are 48 px high with a 1 px border.

### Components and patterns

- **Field:** label above the field in `primary`, 14 px, with `*` when required; placeholder with an example value (for example `Ej: ABC123`); help text and error message below the field.
- **Short choices:** segmented buttons (for example Sí / No) and radio cards for two or three options.
- **Primary call to action:** `cta` pill, disabled until the step is valid; a short expectation text above it and the terms link below it when applicable.
- **Plan cards:** shown side by side on desktop and stacked on mobile; each has a badge, name, subtitle, price, action and coverage list with highlighted amounts. The recommended plan has a `primary` border, `surface-info` background and a text badge.
- **Logo:** the official SURA logo when provided; a text placeholder until then.

## Components and styling

- Spartan UI components are used first; layouts and spacing use Tailwind utilities.
- Colors, spacing and typography come from the design tokens (CSS custom properties); no hard-coded colors and no inline styles.
- The recommended plan (US-02) is distinguished with a visible text label in addition to its styling.

# Design

How the interface looks and behaves. It makes principle P6 concrete and applies the [principles](../.roclec/constitution.md), [ADR-001](adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md), the [architecture](architecture.md) and the [engineering conventions](engineering.md); UI technologies are in [docs/stack.md](stack.md).

## Accessibility

The target is WCAG 2.2 level AA. In this product that means:

- The whole wizard can be completed with the keyboard only, in a logical tab order and without keyboard traps.
- Focus is always visible and never hidden behind other content.
- Every field has a programmatic label. Help text and error messages are associated with their field.
- When a step cannot advance, focus moves to the first invalid field and the error is announced.
- When the step changes, focus moves to the new step's heading; the progress indicator marks the current step.
- Loading, error and empty states are announced to assistive technologies.
- Color is never the only way to convey meaning: the recommended plan, the selected plan and errors also have text or an icon with a label.
- Text and interface elements meet AA contrast; interactive targets are at least 24 × 24 CSS pixels.
- Motion respects the person's reduced-motion preference.

## Responsive design

- Mobile-first. Reference widths: 375 px (mobile) and 1280 px (desktop).
- Content reflows down to 320 px wide without horizontal scrolling.
- The wizard, the plan list and the summary work at both reference widths with the same content.

## Visual identity per country

- Each country has its own theme, configured in Strapi on its `Country` entry: primary color, accent color and logo.
- The application applies the theme at runtime as CSS custom properties consumed by the Tailwind and Spartan UI tokens. Layout, components and typography are shared by both countries (ADR-001, P1).
- Theme colors must meet AA contrast with the text placed on them. A missing or invalid theme falls back to a default theme (P3).

## Components and styling

- Spartan UI components are used first; layouts and spacing use Tailwind utilities.
- Colors, spacing and typography come from design tokens (CSS custom properties); no hard-coded colors and no inline styles.
- The recommended plan (US-02) is distinguished with a visible text label in addition to its styling.

## Copy

User-facing copy is in Spanish and comes from Strapi; only the fallback for unavailable content lives in the front end (engineering).

## Design skills

During the design stage (UX specification and prototypes) and when reviewing user interface changes, agents use these skills pinned in `skills-lock.json`:

| Skill | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `ui-ux-pro-max` | Interaction patterns for forms, wizards, plan comparison and states |
| `design-lab` | Alternative prototype variations to compare before choosing one |
| `impeccable` | Critique and polish of the chosen design |
| `web-design-guidelines` | Audit against web interface and accessibility guidelines |

The other pinned skills (`design-taste-frontend`, `frontend-design`) target public marketing pages and are not used for the wizard.

## Verification

Automated accessibility scans run inside the end-to-end tests (verification reference). Keyboard-only completion and the reference widths are checked in every prototype review and user interface review.
