# Design

How the interface looks and behaves. It makes principle P6 concrete and applies the [principles](../.roclec/constitution.md), [ADR-001](adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md), the [architecture](architecture.md) and the [engineering conventions](engineering.md); UI technologies are in [docs/stack.md](stack.md).

## Accessibility

The target is WCAG 2.2 level AA. In this product that means:

- The whole wizard can be completed with the keyboard only, in a logical tab order and without keyboard traps.
- Focus is always visible and never hidden behind other content.
- Every field has a programmatic label. Help text and error messages are associated with their field.
- When a step cannot advance, focus moves to the first invalid field and the error is announced.
- When the step changes, focus moves to the new step's heading; the progress indicator marks the current step.
- Loading, error and empty states are announced to assistive technologies.
- Color is never the only way to convey meaning: the recommended plan, the selected plan and errors also have text or an icon with a label.
- Text and interface elements meet AA contrast; interactive targets are at least 24 × 24 CSS pixels.
- Motion respects the person's reduced-motion preference.

## Responsive design

- Mobile-first. Reference widths: 375 px (mobile) and 1280 px (desktop).
- Content reflows down to 320 px wide without horizontal scrolling.
- The wizard, the plan list and the summary work at both reference widths with the same content.

## Visual identity per country

- Each country has its own theme, configured in Strapi on its `Country` entry: primary color, accent color and logo.
- The application applies the theme at runtime as CSS custom properties consumed by the Tailwind and Spartan UI tokens. Layout, components and typography are shared by both countries (ADR-001, P1).
- Theme colors must meet AA contrast with the text placed on them. A missing or invalid theme falls back to the default theme (P3).
- The seeded themes for Colombia and Chile use the SURA identity below, which today is the same in both countries.

## Design system

The identity and patterns follow SURA's public insurance sites for [Chile](https://seguros.sura.cl/) and [Colombia](https://www.sura.co/seguros).

### Color tokens

| Token | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `primary` | `#2D6DF6` | Header, secondary buttons, field labels, links |
| `primary-strong` | `#0033A0` | Navigation bar, text on the call to action, field values |
| `cta` | `#E3E829` | Background of the primary call to action |
| `cta-foreground` | `#26328C` | Text on the call to action |
| `accent` | `#00AEC7` | Secondary accent |
| `foreground` | `#1C1C24` | Body text |
| `muted` | `#888B8D` | Secondary text |
| `border` | `#B4B4B5` | Field and card borders |
| `disabled` | `#878789` | Disabled controls |
| `danger` | `#DB1A40` | Errors |
| `surface-info` | `#DFEAFF` | Highlighted sections, recommended plan background |
| `surface-cta` | `#F9FAE1` | Soft call-to-action sections |
| `surface-muted` | `#F8F8F8` | Neutral sections |

Contrast rules: `cta` is used only as a background with `cta-foreground` or `primary-strong` text (8:1), never as text on `primary` (3.4:1, below AA for normal text). White on `primary` and `primary` text on white are at the AA limit (4.5:1) and are not lightened.

### Typography

- Font family: `SuraSans` (regular, semibold, bold) when its files are available; otherwise an open fallback of similar shape (`Nunito Sans`), then `sans-serif`.
- Body 16 px; labels and helper text 14 px; headings 24 to 48 px in bold.

### Shape

- Radii: 8, 12, 16 and 24 px; fields and cards use 12 px; buttons are pills (28 px or more).
- Fields are 48 px high with a 1 px border.

### Components and patterns

- **Field:** label above the field in `primary`, 14 px, with `*` when required; placeholder with an example value (for example `Ej: ABC123`); help text and error message below the field.
- **Short choices:** segmented buttons (for example Sí / No) and radio cards for two or three options.
- **Primary call to action:** `cta` pill, disabled until the step is valid; a short expectation text above it and the terms link below it when applicable.
- **Plan cards:** shown side by side on desktop and stacked on mobile; each has a badge, name, subtitle, price, action and coverage list with highlighted amounts. The recommended plan has a `primary` border, `surface-info` background and a text badge.
- **Logo:** the official SURA logo when provided; a text placeholder until then.

## Components and styling

- Spartan UI components are used first; layouts and spacing use Tailwind utilities.
- Colors, spacing and typography come from the design tokens (CSS custom properties); no hard-coded colors and no inline styles.
- The recommended plan (US-02) is distinguished with a visible text label in addition to its styling.

## Copy

User-facing copy is in Spanish and comes from Strapi; only the fallback for unavailable content lives in the front end (engineering).

## Design skills

During the design stage (UX specification and prototypes) and when reviewing user interface changes, agents use these skills pinned in `skills-lock.json`:

| Skill | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `ui-ux-pro-max` | Interaction patterns for forms, wizards, plan comparison and states |
| `design-lab` | Alternative prototype variations to compare before choosing one |
| `impeccable` | Critique and polish of the chosen design |
| `web-design-guidelines` | Audit against web interface and accessibility guidelines |

The other pinned skills (`design-taste-frontend`, `frontend-design`) target public marketing pages and are not used for the wizard.

## Verification

Automated accessibility scans run inside the end-to-end tests (verification reference). Keyboard-only completion and the reference widths are checked in every prototype review and user interface review.

# Skill name

Copy this template to `.agents/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`, where `<skill-name>` is the reference ID. Register the directory with `reference add <skill-name> --path .agents/skills/<skill-name> --role skill --component NAME` and agree it with `foundation agree --ref <skill-name>`. Its fingerprint covers every file in the directory: editing any of them makes it stale until it is agreed again. `roclec skills` copies it to `.claude/skills/`; edit only the canonical folder under `.agents/skills/`, never the copy.

## Purpose

What project knowledge this skill encapsulates and the problem it prevents.

## Applies to

- Stages: list them in the `skills` key of each stage in `.roclec/flow.toml`; a skill no stage lists applies to every stage.
- Components: the `--component` values of its reference.

## Authority

References and ADRs this skill puts into practice, cited by ID and path. Do not restate their content; when they change, this skill follows them.

- `reference-id` (`path/to/reference.md`)
- `ADR-NNN` (`docs/adr/ADR-NNN-title.md`)

## Conventions or procedure

The rules or steps an agent applies, stated so that they can be checked.

## Examples

Short examples of correct application, and of a common mistake if useful.

## Verification

How a reviewer checks that the work followed this skill. A reviewer may record a finding for each unmet point.

## El problema

- Roclec exige que las skills propias vivan en `.agents/skills/<id>/`. Es la fuente; la copia en `.claude/skills/<id>/` la genera `roclec skills`.
- La línea 12 del `.gitignore` ignora **`.agents` completo** (D-10).
- Por eso una skill propia no llegaría a Git. En un clon faltaría su fuente: `foundation check` y el gate de implement fallarían con `FOUNDATION_INCOMPLETE`, y la copia de `.claude/` no coincidiría con nada.

Hoy `.agents/skills/` contiene 17 skills `roclec-*`, instaladas por Roclec, y las 6 externas de `skills-lock.json`.

## Opciones

| Opción | Cambio en `.gitignore` | A favor | En contra |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A) Ignorar solo lo ajeno** | Quitar `.agents` y añadir `.agents/skills/roclec-*/` y las 6 externas por nombre | Las skills propias se versionan sin hacer nada más. Las de Roclec y las externas siguen fuera, porque se regeneran con `roclec skills --restore` | Al fijar una skill externa nueva hay que añadir su línea |
| **B) Versionar todo `.agents`** | Quitar `.agents` | Lo más simple, y Codex tiene todo en un clon | Revierte D-10 y duplica en Git los ~45 MB de skills externas que ya están en `.claude/skills/` |
| **C) Dejarlo como está** | Nada | — | La skill propia no se versiona y un clon queda bloqueado |

**Recomiendo A.** Mantiene la intención de D-10 (no versionar copias de herramientas) y solo versiona lo que es del proyecto.

Si eliges A, el bloque quedaría así:

.agents/skills/frontend-design/
.agents/skills/impeccable/
.agents/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/
.agents/skills/web-design-guidelines/
.codex

# Angular Skills

The Angular skills are designed to help coding agents create applications aligned with the latest versions of Angular, best practices, new features and manage Angular applications effectively. These skills provide architectural guidance, generate idiomatic Angular code, and help scaffold new projects using modern best practices.

## Available Skills

- **`angular-developer`**: Generates Angular code and provides architectural guidance. Useful for creating components, services, HTTP communication, or obtaining best practices on reactivity (signals, linkedSignal, resource, httpResource), queries and content projection, forms, dependency injection, routing, SSR, accessibility (ARIA), animations, styling, testing, or CLI tooling.
- **`angular-new-app`**: Creates a new Angular app using the Angular CLI. Provides important guidelines for effectively setting up and structuring a modern Angular application.

## Using Agent Skills

Agent Skills are designed to be used with agentic coding tools like [Gemini CLI](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/), [Antigravity](https://antigravity.google/docs/skills) and more. Activating a skill loads the specific instructions and resources needed for that task.

To use these skills in your own environment you may follow the instructions for your specific tool or use a community tool like [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/).

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/angular/skills
```

## Contributions

We welcome contributions to the Angular agent skills. If you would like to contribute to the skills, please make the updates directly in `angular/angular` repository, and to that repository will be output here as a part of our infrastructure setup.

### Feedback & Issues

If you encounter a bug, have feedback, or want to suggest an improvement to the skills, please file an issue in the [angular/angular](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/new?template=3-docs-bug.yaml) issue tracker. Providing detailed context will help us address your feedback effectively.

### Features & Changes (Pull Requests)

We also accept pull requests for new features, updates, or bug fixes for the skills:

1. Make your changes within the `skills/dev-skills/` directory.
2. Follow the standard Angular [Commit Guidelines](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md) and [Coding Standards](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/coding-standards.md).
3. Submit a Pull Request to the main `angular/angular` repository.

---
name: strapi-docs-mcp
description: Query the official Strapi documentation through the strapi-docs MCP server (powered by Kapa). Use for any Strapi question — API syntax, configuration, features, plugins, upgrades, CLI. If the server is missing, instruct the user how to install it.
---

# Strapi docs MCP server

The `strapi-docs` MCP server (URL: `https://strapi-docs.mcp.kapa.ai`) exposes the full Strapi documentation (guides, API references, code examples). Prefer it over training data for Strapi answers, which may be outdated.

Canonical source: https://docs.strapi.io/cms/ai/docs-mcp-server

## Step 1 — Detect availability

Check whether a `strapi-docs` MCP server / tool is connected in the current environment.

- **Available** → go to *Use it*.
- **Not available** → go to *Install it*.

## Available: Use it

Call the `strapi-docs` MCP tools to answer Strapi questions. Pass the user's question directly; quote exact API names, config keys, and versions returned. Cite doc links in the answer.

## Not available: Install it

Add a remote HTTP MCP server named: `strapi-docs` (URL `https://strapi-docs.mcp.kapa.ai`) to the host tool's MCP config, using its standard format. The server uses **OAuth** — the user completes an auth flow on first connection. Then have them reload/restart so it connects.

Per-tool config formats: https://docs.strapi.io/cms/ai/docs-mcp-server#connection-details

## Last resort: Query the docs content directly

If the MCP server is unavailable **and** can't be installed, fall back to the public documentation content. No authentication is required for any of these. Prefer them in this order.

### 1. Per-page Markdown (simplest — add `.md` to any page URL)

Any documentation page is available as flat Markdown by appending `.md` to its URL. All layout components (tabs, accordions, API blocks) are resolved to plain text, so nothing is hidden.

- Page URL:     `https://docs.strapi.io/cms/backend-customization/controllers`
- Markdown URL: `https://docs.strapi.io/cms/backend-customization/controllers.md`
- Pattern: append `.md` to any `https://docs.strapi.io/<page-path>`

This is the same content the docs site's **Copy Markdown** button uses.

### 2. LLMs text files (best when you need many pages at once — flat, nothing hidden)

These follow the [llms.txt convention](https://llmstxt.org/) and are the most agent-friendly source: content is flattened to plain Markdown, so nothing is hidden inside tabs or accordions.

| File | URL | Use for |
|------|-----|---------|
| Index | `https://docs.strapi.io/llms.txt` | Discover every page: a link-rich list of all pages with one-line summaries. |
| Full content | `https://docs.strapi.io/llms-full.txt` | The entire documentation in a single file. Fetch once, then search/grep in it. |
| Code only | `https://docs.strapi.io/llms-code.txt` | All code examples, grouped by page. |

  **Constructing a page URL from `llms.txt`:** entries are protocol-relative paths like `//cms/backend-customization/controllers`. Prepend the docs origin to get the live page as follows:

`//cms/backend-customization/controllers` becomes `https://docs.strapi.io/cms/backend-customization/controllers`

### 3. Raw Markdown source on GitHub (per-page, authoritative)

Each page is a `.md`/`.mdx` file in [`strapi/documentation`](https://github.com/strapi/documentation). Use this only if `docs.strapi.io` itself is unreachable. Build the raw URL from the page path:

===

name: angular-developer
description: Generates Angular code and provides architectural guidance. Trigger when creating projects, components, services, or HTTP communication, or for best practices on reactivity (signals, linkedSignal, resource, httpResource), queries and content projection, forms, dependency injection, routing, server and hybrid rendering (SSR, prerendering, hydration), accessibility (ARIA), animations, styling (component styles, Tailwind CSS), testing, naming conventions, or CLI tooling.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: Copyright 2026 Google LLC
  version: '1.0'
---

# Angular Developer Guidelines

1. Always analyze the project's Angular version before providing guidance, as best practices and available features can vary significantly between versions. If creating a new project with Angular CLI, do not specify a version unless prompted by the user.

2. When generating code, follow Angular's style guide and best practices for maintainability and performance. Use the Angular CLI for scaffolding components, services, directives, pipes, and routes to ensure consistency.

3. Once you finish generating code, run `ng build` to ensure there are no build errors. If there are errors, analyze the error messages and fix them before proceeding. Do not skip this step, as it is critical for ensuring the generated code is correct and functional.

## Creating New Projects

If no guidelines are provided by the user, here are some default rules to follow when creating a new Angular project:

1. Use the latest stable version of Angular unless the user specifies otherwise.
2. Use Signal Forms for form management in new projects (stable in Angular v22 and newer) [Find out more](references/signal-forms.md).

**Execution Rules for `ng new`:**
When asked to create a new Angular project, you must determine the correct execution command by following these strict steps:

**Step 1: Check for an explicit user version.**

- **IF** the user requests a specific version (e.g., Angular 15), bypass local installations and strictly use `npx`.
- **Command:** `npx @angular/cli@<requested_version> new <project-name>`

**Step 2: Check for an existing Angular installation.**

- **IF** no specific version is requested, run `ng version` in the terminal to check if the Angular CLI is already installed on the system.
- **IF** the command succeeds and returns an installed version, use the local/global installation directly.
- **Command:** `ng new <project-name>`

**Step 3: Fallback to Latest.**

content.text:
Revisé los dos repositorios que propones. No he cambiado nada, salvo el `.gitignore`, que sigue sin commit.

## Qué contienen

| Repo | Skill | Contenido | Estado |
|---|---|---|---|
| `angular/skills` | **`angular-developer`** | Guía oficial de Angular, con 45 referencias: signals, `resource`/`httpResource`, **Signal Forms**, DI, routing, accesibilidad (ARIA), **Tailwind**, testing, naming conventions | Licencia MIT. Se genera desde `angular/angular` y recibe commits casi a diario (el último, hoy) |
| | `angular-new-app` | Cómo crear la app con la CLI | Útil solo para el scaffold |
| `strapi/skills` | **`strapi-docs-mcp`** | Consultar la documentación oficial de Strapi con su servidor MCP (`strapi-docs.mcp.kapa.ai`, con OAuth). Si no está, usa las páginas `.md` y `llms.txt` de docs.strapi.io | Último commit en julio. Las demás skills del repo son para MCP o upgrades, o están marcadas *in-progress* |

**Un dato útil:** `angular-developer` dice que **Signal Forms son estables desde Angular v22**. Encaja con el stack («Angular 21 or later»): basta con usar la última versión estable, y desaparece el riesgo de API experimental que anoté.

## Por qué no reemplazan a una skill propia

Son **skills externas**: se fijan en `skills-lock.json`, como las 6 de diseño, y van ignoradas en `.agents/` y versionadas en `.claude/skills/`. Enseñan **Angular y Strapi en general**, pero no saben nada de **este proyecto**:
- ADR-001: `Country`, prefijo de URL, pasos por país.
- La arquitectura: contenedor y presentacional, `src/api/quote`, permisos en el bootstrap.
- Los tokens SURA de diseño y las reglas de verificación (`AC-NN`, ambos países).

Ese conocimiento propio es lo que encapsulan las skills propias (`country-content`, `wizard-feature`, `story-spec`). Además, la clave `skills` de `flow.toml` **solo acepta skills propias registradas**, así que tu elección de «limitar por etapa» aplica a ellas. Las externas se citan desde los documentos, como hicimos en `design.md`.

**Riesgo de las externas, ya vivido en la entrada 6:** `angular/skills` cambia a diario. El hash que fijemos dejará de coincidir pronto y `skills --restore` fallará en un clon limpio. Las copias de `.claude/skills/` sí van en Git, así que Claude Code las tendrá igual; solo afecta a `.agents/`, que usa Codex.

**Recomiendo ambas cosas:**
1. Fijar `angular-developer` y `strapi-docs-mcp`. `angular-new-app` es opcional, solo sirve para el scaffold.
2. Crear las skills propias que elijas, que citarán a las externas en vez de repetir la guía general.

lines: +description: Generates Angular code and provides architectural guidance. Trigger when creating projects, components, services, or HTTP communication, or for best practices on reactivity (signals, linkedSignal, resource, httpResource), queries and content projection, forms, dependency injection, routing, server and hybrid rendering (SSR, prerendering, hydration), accessibility (ARIA), animations, styling (component styles, Tailwind CSS), testing, naming conventions, or CLI tooling.

+1. Always analyze the project's Angular version before providing guidance, as best practices and available features can vary significantly between versions. If creating a new project with Angular CLI, do not specify a version unless prompted by the user.

+2. When generating code, follow Angular's style guide and best practices for maintainability and performance. Use the Angular CLI for scaffolding components, services, directives, pipes, and routes to ensure consistency.

+3. Once you finish generating code, run `ng build` to ensure there are no build errors. If there are errors, analyze the error messages and fix them before proceeding. Do not skip this step, as it is critical for ensuring the generated code is correct and functional.
+If no guidelines are provided by the user, here are some default rules to follow when creating a new Angular project:
+1. Use the latest stable version of Angular unless the user specifies otherwise.
+2. Use Signal Forms for form management in new projects (stable in Angular v22 and newer) [Find out more](references/signal-forms.md).
+When asked to create a new Angular project, you must determine the correct execution command by following these strict steps:
+**Step 1: Check for an explicit user version.**
+- **IF** the user requests a specific version (e.g., Angular 15), bypass local installations and strictly use `npx`.
+**Step 2: Check for an existing Angular installation.**
+- **IF** no specific version is requested, run `ng version` in the terminal to check if the Angular CLI is already installed on the system.
+- **IF** the command succeeds and returns an installed version, use the local/global installation directly.
+- **IF** no specific version is requested AND the `ng version` command fails (indicating no Angular installation exists), you must use `npx` to fetch the latest version.
+When working with Angular components, consult the following references based on the task:
+- **Fundamentals**: Anatomy, metadata, core concepts, self-closing tags, and template control flow (@if, @for, @switch). Read [components.md](references/components.md)
+- **Inputs**: Signal-based inputs, transforms, and model inputs. Read [inputs.md](references/inputs.md)
+- **Outputs**: Signal-based outputs and custom event best practices. Read [outputs.md](references/outputs.md)
+- **Host Elements**: Host bindings and attribute injection. Read [host-elements.md](references/host-elements.md)

+- **Naming Conventions**: Modern Angular v20+ naming style ("Intent over Role") for files, components, services, directives, pipes, and models. Read [naming-conventions.md](references/naming-conventions.md)

+- **Queries and Content Projection**: Signal-based view and content queries (viewChild, viewChildren, contentChild, contentChildren) and content projection with `<ng-content>` slots and fallback content. Read [queries-and-projection.md](references/queries-and-projection.md)
+- **Deferrable Views**: Lazy loading, code splitting, triggers, prefetching, loading states, SSR, and layout stability with `@defer`. Read [deferrable-views.md](references/deferrable-views.md)
+- **Error Boundaries**: Catching render and change detection errors in a template subtree with `@boundary`/`@error`, retrying with `$reset`. Read [error-boundary.md](references/error-boundary.md)

+**Template expressions**: Avoid expensive work in templates (e.g. building arrays or objects, filtering, sorting), since it re-runs on every change detection cycle. Reading signals (`count()`) and cheap calls are fine. Derive other values with `computed()`, a pure pipe, or a child component. See [Avoiding expensive work in templates](references/components.md#avoiding-expensive-work-in-templates).
+If you require deeper documentation not found in the references above, read the documentation at `https://angular.dev/guide/components`.
+When managing state and data reactivity, use Angular Signals and consult the following references:
+- **Signals Overview**: Core signal concepts (`signal`, `computed`), reactive contexts, and `untracked`. Read [signals-overview.md](references/signals-overview.md)
+- **Dependent State (`linkedSignal`)**: Creating writable state linked to source signals. Read [linked-signal.md](references/linked-signal.md)
+- **Async Reactivity (`resource`)**: Fetching asynchronous data directly into signal state. Read [resource.md](references/resource.md)
+- **Side Effects (`effect`)**: Logging, third-party DOM manipulation (`afterRenderEffect`), and when NOT to use effects. Read [effects.md](references/effects.md)
+When communicating with backend services, use Angular HTTP APIs and consult the following reference:
+- **HTTP Client and Resources**: `provideHttpClient`, `HttpClient`, interceptors, and `httpResource`. Read [http-client.md](references/http-client.md)
+In most cases for new apps, **prefer signal forms**. When making a forms decision, analyze the project and consider the following guidelines:
+- If the application is using v22 or newer and this is a new form, **prefer Signal Forms**.
+- For older applications or when working with existing forms, use the appropriate form type that matches the applications current form strategy.
+- **Signal Forms**: Use signals for form state management. Read [signal-forms.md](references/signal-forms.md)
+- **Template-driven forms**: Use for simple forms. Read [template-driven-forms.md](references/template-driven-forms.md)
+- **Reactive forms**: Use for complex forms. Read [reactive-forms.md](references/reactive-forms.md)
+When implementing dependency injection in Angular, follow these guidelines:
+- **Fundamentals**: Overview of Dependency Injection, services, and the `inject()` function. Read [di-fundamentals.md](references/di-fundamentals.md)
+- **Creating and Using Services**: Creating services, the `providedIn: 'root'` option, and injecting into components or other services. Read [creating-services.md](references/creating-services.md)
+- **Defining Dependency Providers**: Automatic vs manual provision, `InjectionToken`, `useClass`, `useValue`, `useFactory`, and scopes. Read [defining-providers.md](references/defining-providers.md)
+- **Injection Context**: Where `inject()` is allowed, `runInInjectionContext`, and `assertInInjectionContext`. Read [injection-context.md](references/injection-context.md)

+- **Hierarchical Injectors**: The `EnvironmentInjector` vs `ElementInjector`, resolution rules, modifiers (`optional`, `skipSelf`), and `providers` vs `viewProviders`. Read [hierarchical-injectors.md](references/hierarchical-injectors.md)

+When formatting values in templates, creating custom pipes, or reusing pipe-like logic in TypeScript, consult the following reference. Prefer pipes in templates; outside templates, avoid injecting pipe classes just to call `transform()`.

+- **Pipes**: Built-in pipe imports, custom pipe naming and implementation, pure vs impure pipes, and TypeScript reuse patterns using standalone formatting functions or extracted plain functions. Read [pipes.md](references/pipes.md)
+When building accessible custom components for any of the following patterns: Accordion, Listbox, Combobox, Menu, Tabs, Toolbar, Tree, Grid, consult the following reference:

+- **Angular Aria Components**: Building headless, accessible components (Accordion, Listbox, Combobox, Menu, Tabs, Toolbar, Tree, Grid) and styling ARIA attributes. Read [angular-aria.md](references/angular-aria.md)
+When implementing navigation in Angular, consult the following references:
+- **Define Routes**: URL paths, static vs dynamic segments, wildcards, and redirects. Read [define-routes.md](references/define-routes.md)
+- **Route Loading Strategies**: Eager vs lazy loading, and context-aware loading. Read [loading-strategies.md](references/loading-strategies.md)
+- **Show Routes with Outlets**: Using `<router-outlet>`, nested outlets, and named outlets. Read [show-routes-with-outlets.md](references/show-routes-with-outlets.md)
+- **Navigate to Routes**: Declarative navigation with `RouterLink` and programmatic navigation with `Router`. Read [navigate-to-routes.md](references/navigate-to-routes.md)
+- **Control Route Access with Guards**: Implementing `CanActivate`, `CanMatch`, and other guards for security. Read [route-guards.md](references/route-guards.md)
+- **Data Resolvers**: Pre-fetching data before route activation with `ResolveFn`. Read [data-resolvers.md](references/data-resolvers.md)
+- **Router Lifecycle and Events**: Chronological order of navigation events and debugging. Read [router-lifecycle.md](references/router-lifecycle.md)
+- **Rendering Strategies**: Choosing between CSR, SSG (prerendering), and SSR. Read [rendering-strategies.md](references/rendering-strategies.md)

+- **Server and Hybrid Rendering**: Implementing server routes, prerendering, hydration, server-compatible code, and request data in an SSR-configured app. Read [server-side-rendering.md](references/server-side-rendering.md)
+- **Route Transition Animations**: Enabling and customizing the View Transitions API. Read [route-animations.md](references/route-animations.md)
+If you require deeper documentation or more context, visit the [official Angular Routing guide](https://angular.dev/guide/routing).
+When implementing styling and animations in Angular, consult the following references:
+- **Using Tailwind CSS with Angular**: Integrating Tailwind CSS into Angular projects. Read [tailwind-css.md](references/tailwind-css.md)
+- **Angular Animations**: Using native CSS (recommended) or the legacy DSL for dynamic effects. Read [angular-animations.md](references/angular-animations.md)
+- **Styling components**: Best practices for component styles and encapsulation. Read [component-styling.md](references/component-styling.md)
+When writing or updating tests, consult the following references based on the task:
+- **Fundamentals**: Best practices for unit testing (Vitest), async patterns, and `TestBed`. Read [testing-fundamentals.md](references/testing-fundamentals.md)
+- **Component Harnesses**: Standard patterns for robust component interaction. Read [component-harnesses.md](references/component-harnesses.md)
+- **Router Testing**: Using `RouterTestingHarness` for reliable navigation tests. Read [router-testing.md](references/router-testing.md)
+- **End-to-End (E2E) Testing**: Setting up and running E2E tests. Read [e2e-testing.md](references/e2e-testing.md)
+When working with Angular tooling, consult the following references:
+- **Angular CLI**: Creating applications, generating code (components, routes, services), serving, and building. Read [cli.md](references/cli.md)
+- **Code Modernization**: Automatically refactoring to modern standards using migrations. Read [migrations.md](references/migrations.md)
+- **Angular MCP Server**: Available tools, configuration, and experimental features. Read [mcp.md](references/mcp.md)
+- **Environment Configuration**: Strategies for build-time and runtime configuration. Read [environment-configuration.md](references/environment-configuration.md)
+When animating elements in Angular, **first analyze the project's Angular version** in `package.json`.

+For modern applications (**Angular v20.2 and above**), prefer using native CSS with `animate.enter` and `animate.leave`. For older applications, you may need to use the deprecated `@angular/animations` package.
+Modern Angular provides `animate.enter` and `animate.leave` to animate elements as they enter or leave the DOM. They apply CSS classes at the appropriate times.

+Use these directly on elements to apply CSS classes during the enter or leave phase. Angular automatically removes the enter classes when the animation completes. For `animate.leave`, Angular waits for the animation to finish before removing the element from the DOM.
+/* Ensure you have a starting style if using transitions instead of keyframes */
+_Note: `animate.leave` may be added to child elements being removed._
+You can bind to `(animate.enter)` and `(animate.leave)` to call functions or use JS libraries like GSAP.
+  // CRITICAL: You MUST call animationComplete() when done so Angular removes the element!
+CSS offers robust tools for advanced animation sequences.
+Toggle CSS classes on elements using property binding to trigger transitions.
+You can use `css-grid` to animate to auto height.
+- **Staggering**: Use `animation-delay` or `transition-delay` with different values for items in a list.
+- **Parallel**: Apply multiple animations in the `animation` shorthand (e.g., `animation: rotate 3s, fade-in 2s;`).
+Retrieve animations directly using standard Web APIs:
+For older projects (pre v20.2 or where `@angular/animations` is already heavily used), you use the component metadata DSL.
+**Important:** Do not mix legacy animations and `animate.enter`/`leave` in the same component.

+The Angular CLI (`ng`) is the primary tool for managing an Angular workspace. Always prefer CLI commands over manual file creation or generic `npm` commands when modifying project structure or adding Angular-specific dependencies.
+**ALWAYS use `ng add` for Angular libraries** instead of `npm install`. `ng add` installs the package AND runs initialization schematics (e.g., configuring `angular.json`, updating root providers).
+To update the application and its dependencies (which automatically runs code migrations):
+ng update @angular/core@<latest or specific version> @angular/cli@<latest or specific version>
+Always use the CLI to generate code to ensure it adheres to Angular standards and updates necessary configuration files automatically.
+| Component    | `ng g c path/to/name` | Generates a component. Use `--inline-style` (`-s`) or `--inline-template` (`-t`) if requested. |
+| Service      | `ng g s path/to/name` | Generates an `@Service` service.                                                               |
+| Directive    | `ng g d path/to/name` | Generates a directive.                                                                         |
+| Pipe         | `ng g p path/to/name` | Generates a pipe.                                                                              |
+| Guard        | `ng g g path/to/name` | Generates a functional route guard.                                                            |
+| Environments | `ng g environments`   | Scaffolds `src/environments/` and updates `angular.json` with file replacements.               |
+_Note: There is no command to generate a single route definition. Generate a component, then manually add it to the `Routes` array in `app.routes.ts`._
+Start the local development server with hot-module replacement (HMR):
+To proxy API requests during development (e.g., rerouting `/api` to a local Node server):
+Compile the application into an output directory (default: `dist/<project-name>/browser`). Modern Angular uses the `@angular/build:application` builder (esbuild-based).
+- `ng build` defaults to the production configuration, which enables Ahead-of-Time (AOT) compilation, minification, and tree-shaking.
+- Target specific configurations defined in `angular.json` using `--configuration`: `ng build --configuration=staging`.
+- **Unit Tests**: Run `ng test` to execute unit tests via the configured test runner (e.g., Karma or Vitest).

---
name: country-content
description: Load when planning, implementing or reviewing a change that adds or modifies country-specific content in Strapi (content types, fields, wizard steps, plans, terms, themes, seed data) or the code that reads it.
---

# Country content

## Purpose

Every wizard screen depends on content that differs by country and is edited by the business team in Strapi. This skill is the repeatable procedure to add or change that content end to end, from the Strapi model to the tests, so that no change breaks the single build for both countries or exposes more than the public role should.

## Applies to

- Stages: plan, implement and review (declared in `.roclec/flow.toml`).

lines: +description: Load when planning, implementing or reviewing a change that adds or modifies country-specific content in Strapi (content types, fields, wizard steps, plans, terms, themes, seed data) or the code that reads it.

+Every wizard screen depends on content that differs by country and is edited by the business team in Strapi. This skill is the repeatable procedure to add or change that content end to end, from the Strapi model to the tests, so that no change breaks the single build for both countries or exposes more than the public role should.
+- Stages: plan, implement and review (declared in `.roclec/flow.toml`).
+- External skill `strapi-docs-mcp`: use it for Strapi API, configuration and CLI questions instead of memory.
+1. **Check the decision.** Confirm the change fits ADR-001. A new step type, content that is not scoped by country or a change to how the country is resolved needs a proposed ADR before any code.

+2. **Model it in Strapi.** Create or edit `apps/cms/src/api/<type>/content-types/<type>/schema.json`. Every country-scoped type has a many-to-one relation to `Country` and draft and publish enabled. Reusable groups of fields go in `apps/cms/src/components/<category>/`. Schema files are committed.

+3. **Regenerate and share types.** Regenerate the Strapi TypeScript types and expose them through `packages/shared`. Update the matching Zod schema in `packages/shared` and add unit tests with valid and invalid content.

+4. **Open only what is read.** If the wizard reads the type, add `find` and `findOne` for it to the public role permissions applied in the bootstrap. Any other permission, or one not covered by the architecture reference, requires updating that reference first.
+5. **Seed both countries.** Extend the seed module for Colombia and Chile. The seed runs only when the database is empty, and the two countries keep different step configurations.

+6. **Read it by country.** The front end requests the content filtered by the current country code, sorted by `order` and limited to published (and, where the type has it, active) entries. It validates the response with the shared Zod schema and handles loading, error and empty states.

+7. **Test it.** Unit tests for the schema; component tests with fixtures for both countries; the end-to-end flow covers the change for Colombia and for Chile. Test titles include the acceptance criterion ID.
+Correct: the plan list requests `GET /api/plans?filters[country][code][$eq]=cl&filters[active][$eq]=true&sort=order:asc`, validates it with the shared plan schema and renders whatever plans arrive.
+Mistake: `if (country === 'cl') { showRutField() }`. Country differences must come from content, never from code (P1).
+A reviewer checks, and records a finding for each unmet point:
+- The change fits ADR-001, or a proposed ADR is cited.
+- `schema.json` is committed, with the `Country` relation and draft and publish for country-scoped types.
+- Types in `packages/shared` are regenerated and the Zod schema matches them, with unit tests.
+- Public permissions are only `find`/`findOne` on types the wizard reads, applied in the bootstrap.
+- Seed data covers both countries with different step configurations.
+- Requests filter by country code; no code branches on a specific country.
+- Tests cover both countries and cite acceptance criterion IDs.
+  "reason": "Owner agrees the country-content procedure for country-specific Strapi content, from model to tests.",

# Native record authoring — model_schema 2, profile 3

All JSON rejects duplicate/unknown keys, non-finite values and escaping/symlink content paths. Lists of IDs/components/references are sorted and unique. CAP/REQ/AC/CHG/FUT use at least three digits. RUN and EVD use ULIDs and explicit supersession. The CLI fills `supersedes` per run scope, per observed AC and per reviewer. Distinct change and release scopes do not share predecessors.

`change seal DIR` computes file hashes, snapshot revisions and the proposal digest. `change seal DIR --check` reports pending changes. Author new proposed snapshots under `proposed/CAP-NNN/draft/` and omit their `revision`; list extra semantic files as keys in `semantic.files`. Seal only an external bundle, then import it with `change new`.

## Change bundle

`change new --file /input/change.json` imports validated content inside that input directory. change.json contains model_schema, id, kind (`evolution|fix|refactor`), semantic and proposal_digest. Semantic contains:

- intention: Markdown path, normally proposal.md; files: {path: exact sha256} of intention/supporting semantic files.
- `origins` contains entries with `kind`, `id`, `locator`, `captured` and `criteria`. The supported kinds are `fut|story|issue|incident|request`. Use an ID unique within the change, a source location, a relative Markdown capture path and sorted, unique criterion IDs. A request also requires `actor`. At least one origin is required for approval. `change seal` adds each captured path to `files` and 
- `coverage` contains `criteria` and `derived`. Each criterion entry names `origin` and `criterion` and has exactly one status. Use `covered` with sorted, unique, nonempty `acceptance_ids`, `excluded` with `reason`, `deferred` with an existing FUT ID in `fut`, or draft-only `gap` with `question`. Every origin criterion needs an entry. Each AC that the evolution adds or changes must appear in a cov
- components: explicit configured names.
- bases: [{capability_id, component, revision}]. Revision null means expected absence; otherwise an exact immutable contract SHA. Each affected pair is explicit.
- deltas: add/retire {op, capability_id, requirement_id}; revise adds retire_acceptance_ids and add_acceptance_ids (optional editorial=true only when behavior truly stays identical); replace uses old_requirement/new_requirement.
- proposed: [{capability_id, components, revision}]; import a complete snapshot under proposed/CAP-NNN/SHA/.
- dependencies: [{component, capability_id, revision}] or [{component, release}]. Empty lists are explicit.
- references: [{id, sha256}] pinned to agreed reference bytes.
- `addresses`: when revising a rejected proposal, use `{ "rejection": "DECISION_SHA", "corrections": [{"id": "R-1", "status": "addressed"}] }` to link the rejection and respond to each correction. Use `disputed` with a `reason` when applicable. Approval checks complete structural coverage, while the user decides whether the responses are sufficient.
- `prototypes`: `[{"path": "docs/prototipo.html", "sha256": "SHA"}]` for the prototypes the change cites. `change seal` pins current project bytes. The implement gate requires an approved checkpoint for the current bytes.
- `sessions`: optional sorted, unique EVD IDs of the agent sessions that drafted the bundle; omit it when empty. Each must be an agent session of this change (`change seal` and `change new` check it).
- architecture_decisions: exactly one of {"adrs": [{id, sha256}]} (non-empty, sorted by ADR ID) or {"none": "reason"}. `change seal` fills a missing sha256 from the current ADR file. Optional while drafting; approval requires it and requires each pin to match the current file. Implement, verify and integrate require every cited ADR to be accepted with the pinned content. An integrated change keeps

Fix/refactor has empty deltas/proposed and preserves exact bases. A historical fix adds baseline_release {component, version}. A fix may add fixes [{component, commit, requirement_ids, acceptance_ids, backport}]; commit is 

For an origin of kind `fut`, import the draft first and record its promotion or duplicate relationship to that change before approval. A deferred criterion must cite an existing FUT. Inspect the change for its origins and coverage. `list changes --origin ID` matches the declared ID across all origin kinds and locators. Qualify IDs with the source system when otherwise ambiguous. Existing schema-2 

Approving freezes the imported snapshot and intention under revisions/<proposal_digest>. Editing semantic content creates another digest and requires another explicit approval. For pending participants, preserve completed component obligations; change already integrated behavior with another CHG. Supporting work notes need not become another normative source.

---
name: story-spec
description: Load when drafting or revising the change bundle (spec) of a user story of the car insurance wizard, before it is presented for approval.
---

# Story spec

## Purpose

The user stories describe each wizard screen but leave product decisions open: how the country is chosen, what happens when Strapi fails, inclusive limits, differences between countries. This skill is the repeatable procedure to turn one user story into a change bundle whose acceptance criteria are observable, verifiable and free of silent assumptions, so that it can pass the approve checkpoint.

## Applies to

- Stages: define (declared in `.roclec/flow.toml`).
- Components: `app`.

## Authority

- `context` (`docs/context.md`) and the user stories US-01, US-02 and US-03.
- `principles` (`.roclec/constitution.md`)
- `ADR-001` (`docs/adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md`) and any other accepted ADR.
- `verification` (`docs/verification.md`), for how each acceptance criterion is verified.
- `design` (`docs/design.md`), for accessibility and responsive rules.
- `flow` (`.roclec/flow.toml`): the approve checkpoint criteria CR-004 to CR-008 that the bundle must satisfy.

## Procedure

1. **One story, one change.** Each user story is one change with an origin of kind `story` (for example `US-01`). Capture only the story text the change needs.
2. **List the origin criteria.** Every Gherkin scenario and every business rule of the story is one origin criterion with its own ID.
3. **Run the gap checklist** on the story and record each answer:
   - Country: what differs between Colombia and Chile (documents, identifiers, currency, steps, copy).
   - States: loading, error, empty and content not published; Strapi unavailable.
   - Limits: boundary values, inclusive or exclusive, dates relative to today.
   - Validation: where rules and error messages come from (Strapi) and when they show.
   - Navigation and data: going back, reloading, double submission.
   - Accessibility and responsive behavior that the design reference makes concrete for this screen.
4. **Resolve every gap.** A gap becomes a derived acceptance criterion with its reason, or a question for the owner through `roclec-clarify`. Never fill a gap with an assumption.
5. **Write the acceptance criteria.** One observable behavior per criterion, in Given/When/Then, with limits and error cases stated. Content-dependent behavior is stated for both countries. Each criterion names how it is verified: unit test, end-to-end test or declared manual check. Criteria describe behavior, not components or file names.
6. **Map coverage.** Every origin criterion is covered by acceptance criteria that actually satisfy it, or excluded or deferred with a reason for the owner.
7. **Cite decisions.** Cite every accepted ADR the change depends on. A new architecture decision the story needs is raised as a proposed ADR, never decided inside the spec.

## Examples

Correct: "Given the current year is Y, when the vehicle year is between Y−20 and Y+1 inclusive, then the step accepts it; when it is Y−21 or Y+2, then the field shows the error message configured in Strapi and the step cannot advance. Verified by unit test."

Mistake: "Validate the vehicle year according to the business rules." It repeats the story's ambiguity and cannot be tested.

## Verification

The owner, at the approve checkpoint, and any reviewer check:

- Every origin criterion has a coverage entry whose acceptance criteria actually satisfy it (CR-004).
- Every acceptance criterion states observable behavior with its limits and error cases (CR-005) and names its verification method (CR-006).
- The gap checklist was applied and every gap is a derived criterion or an owner's answer (CR-007).
- Accepted ADRs are cited and no new architecture decision is hidden in the spec (CR-008).

- **Purpose:** convertir una historia en un spec sin suposiciones silenciosas, de modo que pueda pasar el checkpoint de approve.

  5. Los AC se escriben en Given/When/Then, con límites, ambos países y el método de verificación.
  6. Cobertura completa de los criterios de origen.

- **Example:** el AC del año del vehículo bien escrito frente a «validate per business rules».

---
name: country-content
description: Load when planning, implementing or reviewing a change that adds or modifies country-specific content in Strapi (content types, fields, wizard steps, plans, terms, themes, seed data) or the code that reads it.
---

# Country content

## Purpose

Every wizard screen depends on content that differs by country and is edited by the business team in Strapi. This skill is the repeatable procedure to add or change that content end to end, from the Strapi model to the tests, so that no change breaks the single build for both countries or exposes more than the public role should.

## Applies to

- Stages: plan, implement and review (declared in `.roclec/flow.toml`).
- Components: `app` (`apps/cms`, `packages/shared`, `apps/web`, `e2e`).

## Authority

- `ADR-001` (`docs/adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md`)
- `principles` (`.roclec/constitution.md`): P1, P2, P3, P4, P5
- `architecture` (`docs/architecture.md`)
- `engineering` (`docs/engineering.md`)
- `verification` (`docs/verification.md`)
- `design` (`docs/design.md`), for country themes
- External skill `strapi-docs-mcp`: use it for Strapi API, configuration and CLI questions instead of memory.

## Procedure

1. **Check the decision.** Confirm the change fits ADR-001. A new step type, content that is not scoped by country or a change to how the country is resolved needs a proposed ADR before any code.
2. **Model it in Strapi.** Create or edit `apps/cms/src/api/<type>/content-types/<type>/schema.json`. Every country-scoped type has a many-to-one relation to `Country` and draft and publish enabled. Reusable groups of fields go in `apps/cms/src/components/<category>/`. Schema files are committed.
3. **Regenerate and share types.** Regenerate the Strapi TypeScript types and expose them through `packages/shared`. Update the matching Zod schema in `packages/shared` and add unit tests with valid and invalid content.
4. **Open only what is read.** If the wizard reads the type, add `find` and `findOne` for it to the public role permissions applied in the bootstrap. Any other permission, or one not covered by the architecture reference, requires updating that reference first.
5. **Seed both countries.** Extend the seed module for Colombia and Chile. The seed runs only when the database is empty, and the two countries keep different step configurations.
6. **Read it by country.** The front end requests the content filtered by the current country code, sorted by `order` and limited to published (and, where the type has it, active) entries. It validates the response with the shared Zod schema and handles loading, error and empty states.
7. **Test it.** Unit tests for the schema; component tests with fixtures for both countries; the end-to-end flow covers the change for Colombia and for Chile. Test titles include the acceptance criterion ID.

## Examples

Correct: the plan list requests `GET /api/plans?filters[country][code][$eq]=cl&filters[active][$eq]=true&sort=order:asc`, validates it with the shared plan schema and renders whatever plans arrive.

Mistake: `if (country === 'cl') { showRutField() }`. Country differences must come from content, never from code (P1).

## Verification

A reviewer checks, and records a finding for each unmet point:

- The change fits ADR-001, or a proposed ADR is cited.
- `schema.json` is committed, with the `Country` relation and draft and publish for country-scoped types.
- Types in `packages/shared` are regenerated and the Zod schema matches them, with unit tests.
- Public permissions are only `find`/`findOne` on types the wizard reads, applied in the bootstrap.
- Seed data covers both countries with different step configurations.
- Requests filter by country code; no code branches on a specific country.
- Tests cover both countries and cite acceptance criterion IDs.

<!-- roclec-spec-kit:begin -->
## Roclec native workflow

This project uses Roclec profile 3 for immutable capability contracts, explicit changes, component releases and candidate-bound evidence. Read `.roclec/workflow.md`, `.roclec/model.md`, the profile and applicable agreed consumer references. Use `./.roclec/run --json COMMAND ...`; this launcher supplies the configured project root, including in a linked code repo.

Inspect explicit IDs with exactly one canonical selector: `inspect --change CHG-ID`, `inspect --capability CAP-ID`, `inspect --fut FUT-ID`, or `inspect --release VERSION --component NAME`. Do not select by branch guesses or the newest directory. Mutations require explicit scope/component. Keep templates, principles, architecture and product/design decisions consumer-owned. Use approval and integration/publication operations, not editable done states. Current.json is the integrated vector; release.json alone owns release membership; views are generated. Do not edit immutable snapshots, approved revisions, runs, decisions, preparations or publications.

When the user asks to start or resume a Roclec change, load `roclec-coordinator` as the entry point. Use it to choose and execute the appropriate native skills through authorized integration. The coordinator delegates bounded stages to the installed subagent roles `roclec-specifier`, `roclec-implementer` and `roclec-reviewer` when the host supports them, and runs them in sequence itself otherwise. Roles follow their definitions, return Roclec records and open questions, and never approve, integrate or publish. The declared flow in `.roclec/flow.toml` governs delegation and human stops: stop at every checkpoint and `ai = false` stage, and record decisions with the person's own `--criteria` evaluation. Answer status-only requests with read-only inspection. Approval, release membership, runs and reviews must all match the current intent revision; stale evidence remains history. A structured workflow gate is evidence of a blocker, while invalid invocation, IO failure or malformed output is a technical failure. Do not repeat a failed command without an authorized precondition change. A check pass is structural evidence; a run pass does not substitute for coverage, adopted review or actual visual approval. Record decisions only with real provenance. Do not create/push tags, deploy or send messages merely to satisfy a gate. Optional spec-kit aliases use these same native instructions and have no independent authority.

### Authority map

Generated by Roclec from `.roclec/references.json` and `.roclec/flow.toml`; regenerate it with `roclec views --write` or `roclec skills`, never by hand. Follow these agreed authorities. Do not create new conventions, references or skills without registering and agreeing them (`roclec reference add` and `roclec foundation agree`). Load a skill's content only when its stage needs it.

References by role:
- architecture `architecture`: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md); components: all components
- context `context`: [docs/context.md](docs/context.md); components: all components
- design `design`: [docs/design.md](docs/design.md); components: all components
- engineering `engineering`: [docs/engineering.md](docs/engineering.md); components: all components
- principles `principles`: [.roclec/constitution.md](.roclec/constitution.md); components: all components
- process `flow`: [.roclec/flow.toml](.roclec/flow.toml); components: all components
- stack `stack`: [docs/stack.md](docs/stack.md); components: all components
- verification `verification`: [docs/verification.md](docs/verification.md); components: all components

ADRs:
- `ADR-001`: [docs/adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md](docs/adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md); components: all components

Knowledge skills (`.agents/skills/`, copied to `.claude/skills/` by `roclec skills`):
- `country-content`: [.agents/skills/country-content](.agents/skills/country-content); components: all components; stages: plan, implement, review
- `story-spec`: [.agents/skills/story-spec](.agents/skills/story-spec); components: all components; stages: define
<!-- roclec-spec-kit:end -->
===
IDENTICAL
12:Knowledge skills are the consumer's own references with role `skill` in `.agents/skills/ID/`, distinct from the `roclec-*` skills Roclec refreshes. Register one with `reference add ID --path .agents/skills/ID --role skill --component NAME` and have the user agree it with `foundation agree --ref ID --actor ACTOR --reason TEXT --criteria FILE`; any edit to the folder makes it stale until agreed again. `change approve` pins every skill of the change's components, at any stage, in the decision. Implement requires every skill registered for the component, whatever its stages, agreed on its current bytes (`FOUNDATION_INCOMPLETE`); `inspect --change CHG-ID` lists them per component and stage, and the coordinator gives each role those skills by id and path. `roclec skills` copies them to `.claude/skills/` and regenerates the authority map in the managed block of `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`; never edit the copies.
24:Integrate with `integrate prepare ID --component NAME --run RUN-ID --out FILE` then `operation apply FILE` for authorized integration. The affected code repo must be clean, committed and completely classified. New/untracked/ignored inputs must not escape the manifest; declare inputs, generated outputs and explicit excluded patterns. Root AGENTS/CLAUDE and installed skills may need explicit classification as inputs. Operational metadata is outside the code fingerprint, but pending metadata in a code repo still blocks the next final gate until committed. Roclec never commits automatically.
28:Export plans outside affected code repos to avoid introducing uncommitted files. Apply reconstructs plans, rechecks preconditions under a local lock and journals writes. On IO_PARTIAL preserve the journal and use operation inspect/recover; recovery refuses divergence and never rolls back later authority. Verify a dead owner before removing a stale empty lock. Repeated apply returns historical receipts without replaying pointers. A local lock is not distributed coordination.

# Deliverables and Rules

Deliver a Git repository, public or private and shared with whoever sent you the test.

## Deliverables checklist

The repository must contain:

- [ ] The Angular application code and the Strapi project, with seed data for Colombia and Chile.
- [ ] `README.md` with instructions to run the project and any requirements not met.
- [ ] `FLOW.md` with the step by step of the agentic flow and its diagram.
- [ ] A global context file (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or equivalent).
- [ ] Versioned subagent and skill definitions.
- [ ] A specs folder, at least one spec per user story.
- [ ] An ADRs folder, with at least the multi-country strategy ADR.
- [ ] Evidence of code reviews (reports, PR comments or similar) and how they were resolved.
- [ ] Unedited logs or exports of your sessions with the agents.

## Rules

- Use fictitious data only. Do not include real personal data or credentials in the repository.
- If a tool requires a paid plan and you don't have access, use a free alternative and say so.

# Preguntas que debo responder por fase

Esta guía convierte el assessment y el flujo Roclec del proyecto en preguntas concretas. Responde cada pregunta en el artefacto indicado; si una decisión aún no está tomada, déjala como pregunta abierta en la especificación y no la completes por suposición.

| Fase | Preguntas que debo responder | Dónde registrar la respuesta |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Foundation** | ¿Qué decisiones del negocio y del assessment son obligatorias? ¿Qué reglas deben aplicar igual en Colombia y Chile? ¿Qué decisiones de arquitectura necesitan un ADR porque tienen alternativas con consecuencias importantes? | [Contexto](../context.md), [constitución](../../.roclec/constitution.md), [arquitectura](../architecture.md), [ADR correspondiente](../adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md) y referencias registradas en Roclec. |
| **2. Define** | Para cada historia, ¿quién usa la función y qué resultado espera? ¿Qué campos, formatos, límites, estados vacíos, errores y reglas de validación faltan? ¿Qué datos cambian por país y cuáles son comunes? ¿Cómo se comprobará cada criterio de aceptación? | Una especificación por historia en `specs/` (por ejemplo `specs/US-01-...md`), con preguntas abiertas, criterios observables y su forma de verificación. Relaciona la especificación con [las historias de usuario](04-user-stories.md). |
| **3. Approve** | ¿La especificación describe el comportamiento sin ambigüedades? ¿Cada criterio de aceptación tiene una prueba o comprobación manual? ¿Acepto las exclusiones, aplazamientos y decisiones derivadas que aparecen en la propuesta? | Decisión de aprobación de la revisión exacta de la especificación en Roclec. Las respuestas de negocio deben quedar en la especificación; la aprobación no sustituye esas respuestas. |
| **4. Design** | ¿Cómo se ve y se usa cada paso en móvil y escritorio? ¿Qué ocurre al cargar, ante un error, cuando no hay planes y después del pago simulado? ¿La navegación por teclado, el foco, los mensajes y el contraste cumplen el diseño acordado? ¿Se muestra contenido representativo de Colombia y Chile? | [Diseño](../design.md) para reglas reutilizables; prototipo o artefacto de diseño ligado a la especificación para las pantallas de esa historia. |
| **5. Plan** | ¿Qué tareas cubren cada criterio de aceptación? ¿Qué archivos y componente puede tocar cada responsable? ¿Qué contratos deben acordarse antes de trabajar en paralelo? ¿Qué depende de Strapi, Angular o las pruebas e2e? ¿Qué cambios se integran primero? | Plan y tareas de la revisión aprobada en Roclec; decisiones de arquitectura en ADR. Para un equipo de cinco, registrar responsables, rutas asignadas, dependencias, orden de integración y dueño de conflictos en el mismo plan. |
| **6. Implement** | ¿La implementación sigue la especificación aprobada y las decisiones de arquitectura? ¿Se validan los datos de Strapi antes de usarlos? ¿Se mantienen un solo build y una sola aplicación para los dos países? ¿Se usan solo datos ficticios y no se exponen secretos en el navegador? | Cambios en las rutas del componente `app` declaradas por el plan; actualizar la especificación o solicitar una nueva aprobación si cambia el comportamiento acordado. Las reglas comunes de implementación están en [ingeniería](../engineering.md) y [stack](../stack.md). |
| **7. Verify** | ¿Pasan las pruebas unitarias y de compilación configuradas? ¿Cada criterio de aceptación tiene evidencia? ¿Se probaron contenido válido, incompleto e inválido de Strapi, ambos países, persistencia al volver atrás y errores de pago simulado? ¿Se verificaron teclado, lectores de pantalla y tamaños de pantalla definidos? | Evidencia de ejecución de Roclec y pruebas correspondientes en `apps/web`, `apps/cms` y `e2e/tests`; requisitos en [verificación](../verification.md). |
| **8. Review** | ¿Una persona o agente independiente revisó el candidato? ¿Los hallazgos tienen severidad, evidencia y resolución? ¿La revisión cubre las historias y el comportamiento en los dos países? | Informe de revisión Roclec vinculado al candidato; resolver los hallazgos en el código y volver a verificar lo afectado. |
| **9. Integrate** | ¿El candidato integrado es exactamente el que pasó las comprobaciones y revisión? ¿Todos los hallazgos materiales están resueltos o tienen una decisión registrada? ¿El repositorio está limpio y los cambios están clasificados correctamente? | Registro de integración por componente en Roclec; cambios de código ya integrados en el repositorio. |
| **10. Release** | ¿La versión combinada pasa las comprobaciones finales? ¿La evidencia corresponde al contenido que se va a publicar? ¿Qué limitaciones o requisitos pendientes se deben comunicar? ¿La publicación existente coincide con la preparación aprobada? | Preparación, ejecución final y registro de publicación en Roclec; requisitos de entrega en [entregables](06-deliverables-and-rules.md) y retrospectiva en [flow-retro.md](../flow-retro.md). |
| **Retrospectiva del flujo** | ¿Qué parte del flujo no funcionó como se esperaba y cómo se ajustó? ¿En qué puntos se decidió no usar IA y por qué? ¿Qué cambiaría si cinco desarrolladores trabajaran en paralelo? ¿Dónde aparecieron bloqueos, conflictos o esperas de integración? | [Retrospectiva del flujo](../flow-retro.md). No registres ahí decisiones funcionales que deben pertenecer a una especificación o ADR. |

## Preguntas para coordinar cinco desarrolladores

Antes de repartir trabajo en paralelo, contesta estas preguntas en el **plan** de cada cambio:

1. ¿Qué entregable concreto posee cada desarrollador y qué rutas puede modificar?
2. ¿Qué contratos compartidos deben quedar acordados primero (tipos, esquemas, API de Strapi, navegación y estado del wizard)?
3. ¿Qué tareas pueden avanzar en paralelo sin editar los mismos archivos?
4. ¿Quién integra cada parte y en qué orden se resuelven las dependencias?
5. ¿Cómo se detectan y resuelven conflictos de código o de decisiones antes de que se acumulen?
6. ¿Qué comprobaciones debe pasar cada entrega y quién valida el flujo completo Colombia-Chile?

Registra nombres y asignaciones solo cuando el equipo esté definido. Si todavía no existe esa decisión, conserva las preguntas como pendientes. El flujo actual organiza las fases y los checkpoints, pero por sí solo no asigna trabajo ni coordina ramas entre desarrolladores.

## Regla de uso

La ubicación de la respuesta depende de su naturaleza: comportamiento del producto en la especificación; decisión de arquitectura en un ADR; regla visual reutilizable en diseño; reparto de trabajo en el plan; resultado de pruebas, revisión e integración en sus registros Roclec; y aprendizaje del proceso en la retrospectiva. Mantén la [matriz de entregables del assessment](06-deliverables-and-rules.md) como lista oficial de entregas.
====
# Flow retrospective

This file belongs to the project. Roclec creates it once and never overwrites it, so edit it freely.

The "Flow learning" section of the generated flow view (`docs/flow.md`, or the `view` path in `.roclec/flow.toml`) already lists what the records show: flow revisions and the process FUTs they address, rejections by stage, findings, stages without AI and agent sessions. Run `roclec views --write` to refresh it. Use this file for what the records cannot show.

Add one entry per retrospective, newest first. When a reflection leads to a change in the flow, capture it as a process FUT (`fut capture` with scope `process`) and cite it when the flow is agreed again.

## YYYY-MM-DD — Period or release reviewed

### What did not work as expected

- Where the flow caused friction, rework or waiting, and in which stage.

### What would change with a larger team

- Roles, checkpoints or reviews that would need to change with more people.

### AI-use decisions to revisit

- Stages that should move between AI and a person, and why.

# Deliverables and Rules

Deliver a Git repository, public or private and shared with whoever sent you the test.

## Deliverables checklist

The repository must contain:

- [ ] The Angular application code and the Strapi project, with seed data for Colombia and Chile.
- [ ] `README.md` with instructions to run the project and any requirements not met.
- [ ] `FLOW.md` with the step by step of the agentic flow and its diagram.
- [ ] A global context file (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or equivalent).
- [ ] Versioned subagent and skill definitions.
- [ ] A specs folder, at least one spec per user story.
- [ ] An ADRs folder, with at least the multi-country strategy ADR.
- [ ] Evidence of code reviews (reports, PR comments or similar) and how they were resolved.
- [ ] Unedited logs or exports of your sessions with the agents.

## Rules

- Use fictitious data only. Do not include real personal data or credentials in the repository.
- If a tool requires a paid plan and you don't have access, use a free alternative and say so.

content.text:
Decisiones registradas:
- Entregables también en `flow.toml`.
- Sesiones importadas en Roclec, con el email redactado.
- Esqueleto del README ahora.

Empiezo por los entregables. Busqué en el código de Roclec dónde guarda cada registro y con eso armé esta propuesta para el campo `deliverables` de cada etapa:

| Etapa | Entregables (rutas del repo) | Qué es |
|---|---|---|
| foundation | `docs/`, `docs/adr/`, `.roclec/constitution.md`, `.agents/skills/` | Referencias, ADRs, constitución y skills propias |
| define | `.roclec/changes/` | Bundle del cambio: propuesta, ACs, cobertura y contrato propuesto (el spec de cada historia) |
| approve | `.roclec/decisions/` | Tu aprobación con la evaluación de los criterios |
| design | **`docs/prototypes/`** | Prototipo de cada pantalla (la aceptación queda en `.roclec/decisions/`) |
| plan | **`docs/plans/`**, `.roclec/releases/` | Plan y tareas de cada cambio, y su asignación a una release |
| implement | `apps/web/`, `apps/cms/`, `packages/shared/`, `e2e/` | Código y tests |
| verify | `.roclec/runs/` | Ejecución de los checks con su evidencia |
| review | `.roclec/evidence/` | Informe de revisión con hallazgos y resolución |
| integrate | `.roclec/integrations/`, `specs/capabilities/` | Registro de integración y vista legible de los contratos integrados |
| release | `.roclec/releases/` | Preparación y publicación |

**Dos rutas nuevas que decido yo**, porque Roclec las deja al proyecto:
- `docs/prototypes/`: un archivo por cambio, por ejemplo `docs/prototypes/CHG-001.html`.
- `docs/plans/`: plan y tareas por cambio, por ejemplo `docs/plans/CHG-001/plan.md` y `tasks.md`.

**Al aplicarlo:**
- `docs/flow.md` mostrará la columna de entregables, y desde ahí se arma la tabla de `FLOW.md`.
- Editar `flow.toml` exige volver a acordar el flujo con CR-001…CR-003.
- Más adelante habrá que clasificar `docs/prototypes/` y `docs/plans/` en el perfil, cuando existan.
