input.content:
# Agentic flow How a functional user story becomes a QA-ready increment in this repository, which agents and skills take part, and where a person decides. The flow is defined in [`.roclec/flow.toml`](.roclec/flow.toml), agreed by the owner like any other project reference; [`docs/flow.md`](docs/flow.md) is its generated view. This file explains it. When they differ, `flow.toml` wins. ## Tools - **Claude Code** (desktop app) runs every AI step. Model: Claude Opus 5.5, used by the main session and inherited by the subagents. - **Roclec** (spec-driven development framework) keeps the specs, approvals, runs, reviews and integrations as versioned, hash-pinned records under `.roclec/`. The spec is the source of truth: code is verified against the approved spec, and an edit to an agreed spec or reference invalidates it until a person agrees it again. Why this combination: spec-driven development turns each story into verifiable acceptance criteria before any code; Roclec adds what a prompt alone cannot enforce: gates that refuse to implement without an approved spec, approvals tied to the exact content approved, evidence tied to the exact code tested and a review done in a separate context. ## Agents and skills | Who | Definition | Responsibility | | --- | --- | --- | | Coordinator | Main Claude Code session, entry skill `roclec-coordinator` | Runs the flow, talks to the owner, runs foundation, design, integration and release, and delegates the rest | | Specifier | Subagent [`.claude/agents/roclec-specifier.md`](.claude/agents/roclec-specifier.md) | Drafts the spec (change bundle) of a story; never approves | | Implementer | Subagent [`.claude/agents/roclec-implementer.md`](.claude/agents/roclec-implementer.md) | Plans, implements and runs the checks of an approved change; never changes the approved intent | | Reviewer | Subagent [`.claude/agents/roclec-reviewer.md`](.claude/agents/roclec-reviewer.md) | Reviews the candidate in a separate context and records findings; read-only except for its report | | Owner | The person | Agrees references and ADRs, approves specs, accepts prototypes and plans, decides on findings before integration | Each subagent definition declares its instructions, allowed tools, inputs and outputs. Skills: - **Procedure skills** `roclec-*` (installed by Roclec): how to specify, plan, implement, review and integrate. - **Project knowledge skills** (ours, agreed like references): [`story-spec`](.agents/skills/story-spec/SKILL.md) for the specifier in define, [`country-content`](.agents/skills/country-content/SKILL.md) for plan, implement and review. - **Official skills** pinned in `skills-lock.json`: `angular-developer`, `strapi-docs-mcp` and the design skills listed in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md). ## Diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD F["1. Foundation
references, ADRs, skills"] -->|owner agrees| S0(["User story"]) S0 --> D["2. Define
specifier drafts spec"] D --> A{"3. Approve
owner, no AI"} A -->|reject: revise| D A -->|approved| G["4. Design
prototype"] G --> GC{"owner accepts
prototype"} GC -->|reject: revise| G GC -->|accepted| P["5. Plan
implementer"] P --> PI{"owner approves
plan"} PI -->|reject: revise| P PI -->|approved| I["6. Implement
implementer"] I --> V["7. Verify
checks run by Roclec"] V -->|fail| I V --> R["8. Review
reviewer, separate context"] R -->|findings| I R --> IC{"owner checks findings
and checks"} IC -->|reject: revise| I IC -->|approved| N["9. Integrate"] N --> L["10. Release
ready for QA"] classDef human fill:#fde68a,stroke:#92400e; class A,GC,PI,IC human; ``` Foundation runs once and again whenever a reference changes; steps 2 to 10 run once per user story. ## Steps | Step | Description | AI used? | AI, agent, subagent or skill | Deliverable | Human in the loop | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1. Foundation | Agree the references every change depends on: context, principles, stack, architecture, engineering, verification, design, the flow itself, ADRs and knowledge skills. | Yes | Coordinator with `roclec-foundation` and `roclec-constitution`; Claude Opus 5.5 | `docs/`, `docs/adr/`, `.roclec/constitution.md`, `.agents/skills/`; agreements in `.roclec/decisions/` | Owner agrees each document against CR-001 to CR-003. On rejection the coordinator revises it; until agreed, implementation is blocked. | | 2. Define | Turn the story into a spec: origin criteria, gap checklist, acceptance criteria with their verification method, coverage, cited ADRs. Open questions go to the owner. | Yes | Specifier subagent with `roclec-specify`, `roclec-clarify`, `roclec-analyze`, `roclec-checklist` and `story-spec` | Change bundle in `.roclec/changes/CHG-NNN/` | Owner answers the questions the specifier raises; nothing is assumed. | | 3. Approve | Accept the exact spec; approval freezes its digest. | **No** | — | Approval in `.roclec/decisions/` | Owner evaluates CR-004 to CR-008. On rejection: corrections recorded, specifier revises, owner approves the new revision. | | 4. Design | Interaction specification and a prototype of the screen, shown with Colombia's and Chile's content. | Yes | Coordinator with `roclec-ux`, `roclec-prototype` and the design skills | `docs/prototypes/CHG-NNN.html`; acceptance in `.roclec/decisions/` | Owner accepts the prototype against CR-009 and CR-010. On rejection the prototype is revised. | | 5. Plan | Assign the change to a release and plan tasks per acceptance criterion within the component's paths. | Yes | Implementer subagent with `roclec-plan`, `roclec-tasks`, `roclec-release` and `country-content` | `docs/plans/CHG-NNN/`, `.roclec/releases/` | Owner approves the plan before any code (pre-implement, CR-011). On rejection the plan is revised. | | 6. Implement | Write the code and tests of the approved change. | Yes | Implementer subagent with `roclec-implement`, `country-content`, `angular-developer`, `strapi-docs-mcp` | `apps/web/`, `apps/cms/`, `packages/shared/`, `e2e/` | — (bounded by the approved spec and plan). | | 7. Verify | Run the configured checks on the exact candidate and record the evidence per acceptance criterion. | Yes | Implementer subagent; checks executed by Roclec (`run verify`) | `.roclec/runs/` | — (a failing check sends the change back to implement). | | 8. Review | Independent review of the candidate; every finding has a severity and stays open until resolved or decided. | Yes | Reviewer subagent with `roclec-reviewer` and `country-content`, in a context separate from the implementation | Review report in `.roclec/evidence/` | Owner decides any finding the reviewer cannot resolve (accept, fix or defer). | | 9. Integrate | Integrate the verified, reviewed candidate. | Yes | Coordinator with `roclec-converge` | `.roclec/integrations/`, `specs/capabilities/` | Owner checks that findings are resolved and checks pass before integration (pre-integrate, CR-012). On rejection the change goes back to implement. | | 10. Release | Verify the combined release, prepare it and record the Git publication: the increment is ready for QA. | Yes | Coordinator with `roclec-release` | `.roclec/releases/` | Owner asks for the publication; agents never push, tag or deploy on their own. | The criteria CR-001 to CR-012 are listed in [docs/flow.md](docs/flow.md#criteria). Every human decision is recorded with the owner's evaluation of each criterion; agents never fill it in. ## Traceability User story → spec (`.roclec/changes/CHG-NNN/`, origin `US-NN`) → ADRs cited and pinned in the spec → code (the run records the exact files tested) → tests (acceptance criterion IDs in test titles, results in `.roclec/runs/`) → review (`.roclec/evidence/`, linked to the same candidate) → integration (`.roclec/integrations/`). `./.roclec/run inspect --change CHG-NNN` shows the whole thread of one change. ## Session logs Agent sessions are imported into Roclec as evidence (`.roclec/evidence/EVD-*.session`). The only edit is automatic redaction of secrets and email addresses configured in [`.roclec/project.toml`](.roclec/project.toml) (`secret_env`, `redact_patterns`); the original stays local. ## Questions ### At which points did we decide not to use AI, and why? - **Approving a spec** (step 3) is not an AI step: only a person decides which behavior is accepted. - **Every checkpoint decision** (references and ADRs, prototypes, plans, integration) is made by the owner, who evaluates each criterion; agents prepare the material and never record the decision or its evaluation. - **Publishing** (commits on request, push, tags, deploys) is done only when the owner asks. ### What would we do differently with a team of five developers? - Split the work by component and contract: agree shared types, Zod schemas and the Strapi API in `packages/shared` first, then let front-end and CMS work run in parallel. - Give every plan named owners, the paths each may change, dependencies and the integration order. - Add deciders: a product owner approves specs and prototypes, a technical lead accepts ADRs and approves plans, and a peer approves before integration. - Make agent session evidence mandatory again in define, implement and review, so each person's AI work stays auditable. - Add the release handoff checkpoint, so QA accepts the increment explicitly. ### Which part of the flow did not work as expected, and how did we adjust it? - **Generic seeded criteria.** The seeded approval criteria were too vague to reject anything with a clear reason. We rewrote them into twelve specific criteria, one decision point at a time. - **No human gate on the plan.** The seeded flow let the agent go from an approved spec straight to code. We added the pre-implement checkpoint. - **Mixed sources.** Early drafts justified product rules with the test's evaluation rules instead of the product context. Creé el commit `0d4b26b chore(roclec): redact email addresses in session transcripts`.

Ya está el borrador de [FLOW.md](FLOW.md), en inglés, en la raíz del repo. Contiene:

- **Herramientas:** Claude Code con Claude Opus 5.5, y Roclec. Incluye por qué se eligió SDD con Roclec.
- **Agentes y skills:** una tabla con coordinador, specifier, implementer, reviewer y owner, con enlaces a las definiciones en `.claude/agents/`. Luego las skills de procedimiento, las propias y las oficiales.
- **Diagrama Mermaid:** los 4 puntos de decisión humana marcados y los bucles de rechazo.
- **Tabla de los 10 pasos** con las 6 columnas pedidas: paso, descripción, si usa IA, agente o skill, entregable con su ruta, y quién decide y qué pasa al rechazar. Foundation se ejecuta una vez; los pasos 2 a 10, una vez por historia.
- **Trazabilidad:** historia → spec → ADR → código → tests → revisión → integración, con sus rutas.
- **Logs de sesión:** dónde quedan y cuál es la única edición (la redacción).
- **Las 3 preguntas**, respondidas de forma breve.

Revisa especialmente estas partes:

1. **Equipo de 5:** las 5 respuestas son propuesta mía. Siguen tu archivo `08`: primero contratos en `packages/shared`, owners y rutas en cada plan, más decisores, sesiones obligatorias de nuevo y handoff a QA.
2. **Qué no funcionó:** las 6 respuestas salen de lo que pasó en foundation: criterios genéricos, falta de un gate del plan, mezcla de fuentes, orden de las referencias, sesiones obligatorias con privacidad, y skills propias que no se versionaban. Lo redacté sin mencionar el piloto.
3. **Sección «Session logs»:** dice que las sesiones *se importan*, pero todavía no hay ninguna. La importación queda para después del README, como acordamos.

# Car insurance quoting app

A single application that sells car insurance in Colombia and Chile: a three-step wizard (policyholder and vehicle data, plan list, summary and payment) whose fields, plans and copy are configured per country in Strapi. Product context: [docs/context.md](docs/context.md).

**Status:** the project references, ADR-001 and the agentic flow are agreed; the application code does not exist yet.

## Running the project

To be added with the workspace: the whole project will start with `docker compose up`, with seed data for both countries.

## Requirements not met

To be listed when the implementation is complete.

## Repository guide

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Agentic flow, step by step, with its diagram | [FLOW.md](FLOW.md) |
| Global context file for agents | [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) (same content in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)) |
| Subagent definitions | [.claude/agents/](.claude/agents/) |
| Project knowledge skills | [.agents/skills/](.agents/skills/) (copies for Claude Code in `.claude/skills/`) |
| Principles | [.roclec/constitution.md](.roclec/constitution.md) |
| Context, stack, architecture, engineering, verification and design | [docs/](docs/) |
| Architecture decision records | [docs/adr/](docs/adr/) |
| Specs, one per user story | `.roclec/changes/CHG-NNN/`; integrated contracts readable in `specs/capabilities/` |
| Code reviews with findings and resolutions | `.roclec/evidence/` |
| Agent session logs | `.roclec/evidence/EVD-*.session` |
| Application code | `apps/web/` (Angular), `apps/cms/` (Strapi), `packages/shared/`, `e2e/` |

## Agentic flow tooling

- **Claude Code** with Claude Opus 5.5 runs every AI step.
- **Roclec** 0.9.0.dev0 records specs, approvals, runs, reviews and integrations under `.roclec/`. Its CLI runs from a local Python environment through `./.roclec/run` (for example `./.roclec/run --json check`).

[FLOW.md](FLOW.md) explains why this combination was chosen.

## Session logs

Agent sessions are stored as Roclec evidence. The versioned copy is the original transcript with one automatic edit: values of the configured secret environment variables and matches of the configured patterns (tokens and email addresses) are replaced with `[REDACTED]`, as declared in [.roclec/project.toml](.roclec/project.toml). The unredacted original stays local and its hash is recorded with the evidence.

## Data

Only fictitious data is used. No real personal data, card data or credentials are stored in this repository.
